requirements.text: The application for type approval of a vehicle type under UN R148 shall be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by the holder's duly accredited representative.
The application for approval shall be accompanied by the items listed under paragraph 3.1.2 (the enumerated list that follows this paragraph).
The application shall be accompanied by drawings sufficiently detailed to permit identification of the type and, if applicable, of the category of the lamp.
The drawings shall show geometrically in what position(s) the lamp (and, if applicable, the rear window) may be mounted on the vehicle.
The drawings shall show the axis of observation to be taken as the axis of reference in the tests (horizontal angle H = 0°, vertical angle V = 0°).
The drawings shall show the point to be taken as the centre of reference during the tests.
The drawings shall show the limit of the apparent surface of the function(s).
The drawings shall show the space reserved and the arrangement intended for the approval marking.
In case of replaceable source module(s), the drawings shall show the module(s) and the space reserved for the specific identification code(s) of the module(s) on the lamp and on the module(s).
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the drawings shall show the interdependent lamp or the combination of interdependent lamps that fulfil the relevant requirements.
In the case of a lamp that may incorporate a vehicle manufacturer logo, the drawings shall show the vehicle manufacturer logo.
The application shall be accompanied by a brief technical description of the lamp.
For lamps with replaceable UN approved light sources, the technical description shall state the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
For lamps with replaceable light source module(s), the technical description shall state the light source module specific identification code.
The technical description shall state the make and type of electronic light source control gear(s) or variable intensity control(s), if any and if not being part of the lamp.

Where the lamp shall also be approved with LED substitute light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 128, the technical description shall state the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Where a device is intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, the technical description shall contain the specification of the optical properties (transmission, colour, inclination, etc.) of the rear window(s).

Where a lamp may incorporate a vehicle manufacturer logo, the applicant shall confirm, by a statement provided by the vehicle manufacturer, that the vehicle manufacturer logo is the official appropriate one related to the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer.

At the applicant's discretion, the description may specify whether the lamp may be installed on the vehicle with different inclinations of the reference axis in respect to the vehicle reference planes and to the ground, or rotated around its reference axis.
The different conditions of installation specified in the description shall be indicated in the communication form.
Unless otherwise specified for the relevant lamp, the application shall be accompanied by two complete samples of the lamp.

Where applications are made for non-identical but symmetrical lamps suitable for mounting one on the left and one on the right side of the vehicle, the two submitted samples may be identical and suitable for mounting only on the right or only on the left side of the vehicle.
For a variable-intensity lamp, the application shall be accompanied by a sample of the variable intensity control or a generator providing the same signal(s).
A separate approval is required for each lamp listed in paragraph 1 of UN R148.

When two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval of that unit may be granted only if each of these lamps satisfies the provisions set out in UN R148 or in another Regulation.
A lamp that does not satisfy the provisions of UN R148 or of any other Regulation under which it is assessed shall not be part of a grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp unit.
If the type of lamp(s) submitted for approval under paragraph 3.1 meets the requirements of UN R148, approval shall be granted.
All the devices of an interdependent lamp system must be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.

Notice of approval, extension, refusal, withdrawal of approval, or definitive discontinuation of production of a lamp type under this Regulation shall be communicated to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement that apply this Regulation by means of a form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
An approval number shall be assigned to each type of lamp approved.
The approval number assigned to each lamp shall be indicated for each lamp in the communication form in Annex 1.
A contracting party may assign the same approval number to light-signalling devices or systems incorporating a number of lamps.
A contracting party shall not assign the same approval number to another type of lamp of the same function.
The symbol identifying each light signalling lamp (function) for which type approval has been granted shall be the symbol listed for that function in Table 1 (List of symbols).
The applicable change index for each device relating to each series of amendments shall be as specified in Table 2 (Series of amendments and change index), see also paragraph 7.1.1.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and for the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for “a” shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall consist of the elements listed in the subparagraphs that follow this paragraph (the list itself is not included in the provided text).
The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.

The arrow in the additional symbol shall be directed outwards from the vehicle for: direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12; front or rear position lamps; front or rear end-outline marker lamps; and reversing lamps in the case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
On direction indicators of categories 5 and 6 and on combined parking lamps, the arrow shall be directed towards the front of the vehicle.
For direction indicators of category 6, an indication "R" or "L" shall be shown on the lamp, indicating the right or left side of the vehicle.
If applicable, the additional letter shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.
On lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the approval marking shall include the additional letter "D".
On lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system, the approval marking shall include the additional letter "Y".
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, other than lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
Where a lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), the lamp shall also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).

Lamps with an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control, a secondary operating mode, or non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear its specific identification code.

Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, the specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph (the paragraph reference is cut off in the source text).

Where several non-identical light source modules are used, the approval mark on a module need not be the same as the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used, but both marks shall be from the same applicant.
On the light source module, the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage shall be marked.
On the lamp, the specific identification code of the module shall be marked as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a)(ii).
On the lamp, the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage shall be marked.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control that is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

In any case, the approval marking and the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings required by paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings specified in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed.
The single approval mark on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps may be located anywhere on the lamps, provided that the conditions listed after this paragraph are met.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Every modification of a type of lamp shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority that approved the type.
After being notified of a modification of a type of lamp, the Type Approval Authority may take one of the alternative actions listed in the following sub-paragraphs.

Confirmation or refusal of approval, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 3.2.3.1 to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying UN R148.
The Type Approval Authority issuing the extension of approval shall assign a series number for that extension.

The Type Approval Authority issuing the extension of approval shall inform the other Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying the UN Regulation under which the approval has been granted of that extension by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3) of the 1958 Agreement.
The conformity of production procedures shall comply with the requirements set forth in paragraph 6 of UN R148.
The approval granted may be withdrawn if the requirements in UN R148 are not met.

If a Contracting Party to the 1958 Agreement that applies this Regulation withdraws an approval it has previously granted, that Contracting Party shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation of the withdrawal, by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a lamp approved in accordance with UN R148, the holder shall inform the authority which granted the approval.

Upon receiving the holder's communication that production has been definitively discontinued, the authority which granted the approval shall inform the other Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying UN R148 by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.

Each Contracting Party to the 1958 Agreement that applies UN R148 shall communicate to the United Nations Secretariat the names and addresses of the Technical Services responsible for conducting approval tests and of the Type Approval Authorities that grant approval and to which forms certifying approval, extension, refusal or withdrawal of approval, or definitive discontinuation of production issued in other countries are to be sent.
Each lamp submitted for approval under UN R148 shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5 of that regulation.

The requirements of sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and the Annexes referenced in those sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to UN R148.

The requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the vehicle category/ies on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that, in normal conditions of use and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured.
The lamps shall retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation in normal conditions of use and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use.
Front and rear position lamps that are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated may also be used as end-outline marker lamps.

Position lamps or daytime running lamps that are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source and designed to operate permanently with an additional system regulating the intensity of the emitted light, are permitted.

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, the position and stop functions shall be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source).

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, the position and stop functions shall be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp and either alternative (a) or (b) is applied, a note shall be made within the communication document.

If a front position lamp incorporates one or more infrared radiation generators, its photometric and colour requirements shall be met both with and without the operation of the infrared radiation generator(s).

On the applicant's request, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function) may incorporate one manufacturer logo built from transparent or non-transparent components, provided all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation are fulfilled and the conditions (a) to (c) are met.
Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., the logo incorporated in the lamp shall be only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer.
The applicant shall confirm that the logo is only the brand-name logo of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer by a statement as referred to in paragraph 3.1.2.2. (f).

The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of such a lamp, measured in the direction of the reference axis, shall not exceed 100 cm2.

Notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, the logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) need not be symmetrical by itself.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following provisions (a) or (b) shall apply.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3.
When all light sources of a single lamp containing more than one light source are illuminated, the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced.
Where the tell-tale signal option is used, a note in the communication form shall state that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
For daytime running lamps, the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.1.3 replace the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2 and apply in addition to the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1.
When any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, at least one of the provisions (a) or (b) shall apply.

Under option (a), after failure of any one light source in a multi-source lamp, the light intensity at the points of standard light distribution defined in paragraph 2.2. of Annex 3 shall be at least 80 per cent of the minimum intensity required.

Under option (b), after failure of any one light source in a multi-source lamp, a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.19.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced.
Where option (b) is used, a note in the communication form shall state that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12, the provisions of paragraph 4.6.1.4 apply instead of the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2 and in addition to the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1.

A signal for activation of the tell-tale prescribed in paragraph 6.5.8. of Regulation No. 48 or paragraph 6.3.8. of Regulation No. 53 shall be produced on the basis of either option (a), (b) or (c) of paragraph 4.6.1.4, notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The tell-tale activation signal shall be produced when any one light source of the direction-indicator lamp has failed.

For a lamp designed for only two light sources, the tell-tale activation signal shall be produced when the intensity in the axis of reference is less than 50 per cent of the minimum intensity required.

The tell-tale activation signal shall be produced when, as a consequence of a failure of one or more light sources, the intensity in any one of the following directions (as indicated in paragraph 2.1. of Annex 3) is less than the minimum intensity required: (i) H=0°, V=0°; (ii) H=20° outwards to the outside of the vehicle, V=+5°; (iii) H=10° inwards to the inside of the vehicle, V=0°.
In case of failure of the variable intensity control, a rear position lamp of category R2 shall not emit more than the maximum luminous intensity value of category R1.
In case of failure of the variable intensity control, a rear end-outline marker lamp of category RM2 shall not emit more than the maximum luminous intensity value of category RM1.
In case of failure of the variable intensity control, a stop lamp of category S2 shall not emit more than the maximum luminous intensity value of category S1.
In case of failure of the variable intensity control, a stop lamp of category S4 shall not emit more than the maximum luminous intensity value of category S3.
In case of failure of the variable intensity control, a direction indicator of category 2b shall not emit more than the maximum luminous intensity value of category 2a.
In case of failure of the variable intensity control, a rear fog lamp of category F2 shall not emit more than the maximum luminous intensity value of category F1.
In case of failure of the variable intensity control, the steady luminous intensity requirements of the respective lamp category shall be fulfilled automatically.

The lamp shall only be equipped with the following types of light source: (a) replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128; (b) light source module(s); and/or (c) non-replaceable light source(s).

Replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 may be used in the lamp only if no restriction on their use is made at the time of application for type approval.

Where a light source category, categories or type(s) is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, the applicant for type approval of the lamp shall declare that the lamp is only intended for installation on those vehicles.

Where a light source category, categories or type(s) is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, the lamp-only-for-those-vehicles declaration made by the applicant shall be noted in the communication form.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed shall apply.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s) shall apply.
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances that cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module shall be such that it can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

When the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
All photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with respect to the conditions listed following paragraph 4.8.1.
For replaceable UN approved light sources, all measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.

In the case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the standard light source(s) used for measurements shall have a luminous flux value that does not deviate more than 5 per cent from its reference/objective luminous flux value when test voltage is applied.
For a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

For a lamp (function) using light sources subject to more than one of the conditions in paragraph 4.8., the photometric measurements shall be made separately for each applicable condition set forth in paragraph 4.8.

The separate photometric measurement results obtained for each applicable condition of paragraph 4.8. for a lamp (function) with light sources subject to more than one condition shall be added together.
The test laboratory may require the applicant to provide samples that allow the different light source(s) to be supplied separately.
During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position, or in a field of different positions, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.

Where the applicant elects to have the lamp also approved with LED substitute light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be repeated using the prescribed LED substitute light source(s).
Unless otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.

If the results of measurements are challenged, measurements shall be carried out in such a way as to meet the requirements listed under paragraph 4.8.1.8 (the list itself is not included in this paragraph text).
The distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.
The measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver, viewed from the reference centre of the light, is comprised between 10' and 1 degree.

The intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from that direction of observation.
The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
For category 5 and 6 direction indicators, the limits of the light emitting surface shall be determined instead of the apparent surface limits.
The requirement to determine the apparent surface limits shall not apply to rear-registration plate illuminating lamps.

For a lamp intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, the sample plate or sample plates (one per possibility where several exist), as supplied per paragraph 3.1.2.8., shall be positioned in front of the lamp to be tested, in the geometrical position(s) described in the application drawing(s) per paragraph 3.1.2.2.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
Where a lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
The test laboratory may require the electronic light source control gear or the variable intensity control (the source paragraph is truncated, so the required action is not stated).
Where the lamp has light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
For a lamp with replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated at the reference/objective luminous flux during testing.

As an alternative to operating at the reference/objective luminous flux, a lamp with replaceable UN approved light source(s) may be operated at a different luminous flux, provided the measured luminous intensities are corrected proportionally.

The lamp with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources shall be operated at a voltage or electrical current setting such that the actual luminous flux of each light source does not deviate by more than 5 per cent from the average luminous flux of the light sources.

The measured luminous intensities of the lamp with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources shall be corrected proportionally for the difference between the average luminous flux of the light sources and the applicable reference/objective luminous flux.
As an alternative, the lamp may be tested by using one light source in each of the individual lamp holder positions, with each light source operating at the reference/objective luminous flux.
When this alternative test method is used, the sum of the measured luminous intensities for each direction shall be applied.

The identification of an electronic light source control gear (if applicable) or variable intensity control (if applicable) and/or the voltage applied, including the tolerances, shall be noted in the communication form in Annex 1.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. on the reference axis (HV).

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall not exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. in any direction where the lamp is visible.

If not otherwise specified, outside the reference axis the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. and the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, outside the reference axis the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the intensity value specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed when measuring the intensity of light emitted by the samples.
The applicant may request an additional test to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No.48.
In the additional test, the maximum intensity in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall not be more than 2.5∙10-1 cd.
The additional test may be conducted taking into account the influence of the vehicle body.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, the assembly shall comply with the maximum intensity requirements if all lamps together are lit.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, the assembly shall comply with the minimum intensity requirements if either lamp has failed.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

Where the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirement at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

For the rear position lamp system described in (a), the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed to be satisfied if the interdependent lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

Where the interdependent lamp system providing the rear direction indicator function is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirement at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

The requirement for the rear direction indicator function in (b) does not apply to interdependent direction indicator lamp(s) intended for fitting on vehicle(s) where, to fulfil or complete the geometric visibility angle, additional lamps are activated when the movable component is in any fixed open position.

The additional lamps activated in the case described in (b) shall satisfy all the position, photometric and colorimetric requirements applicable to the direction indicator lamps installed on the movable component.

The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities (the specific limits are given in the enumerated items that follow this paragraph, which were not included in the provided text).

For systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals that cause the steady luminous intensity of the lamp to exceed the respective maximum specified in paragraph 5. under night-time conditions.

For systems other than those depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals that cause the steady luminous intensity of the lamp to exceed the respective maximum specified in paragraph 5. under standard conditions.

Where a rear position lamp and/or a rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensity actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp or end-outline marker lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines through ±10° H of the light distribution table.

Where one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated lamps contain more than one light source and are considered as a single lamp, the luminous intensity values to be considered shall be those obtained with all sources in operation.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities of the lamp shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
To check the colorimetric characteristics of the light emitted, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour of the emitted light shall be observed.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked separately for each light source technology according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1 and 4.8.2.
The test laboratory may require the applicant to provide samples that allow the different light source(s) to be supplied separately.

The minimum luminous intensity in cd for signal category A, MA or AM, at the angles of geometric visibility, shall be not less than the value in the table for the applicable lamp configuration (a single lamp, or a lamp marked "D" per 3.3.2.5.2.). The table layout is garbled in the source, so the row-to-value mapping must be checked against the original document.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 4 (luminous intensities for rear position and rear end-outline marker lamps).
For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of 6.0∙101 cd is permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.

A steady R1, MR or RM1 lamp shall provide the minimum luminous intensities in cd given in the table (4∙100, 1.7∙101 and 8.5∙100 cd for the angles of geometric visibility listed in paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d)), measured per Figure A3-I and Table A2-1.

A variable R2 or RM2 lamp shall provide the minimum luminous intensities in cd given in the table (4∙100, 4.2∙101 and 2.1∙101 cd for the angles of geometric visibility listed in paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d)), measured per Figure A3-I and Table A2-1.
The minimum luminous intensity of the rear position lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall meet the values specified in Table 4.
For end-outline marker lamps (RM1, RM2), the standard light distribution may be considered, at the request of the applicant, from the VV line to the outboard side only.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two stop lamp samples supplied shall meet the luminous intensity requirements in Table 7 (luminous intensities for stop lamps).

For the S1 (steady) signal, the luminous intensity shall meet the minimum values in cd given in the table (6.0∙10^1, 2.60∙10^2 and 1.30∙10^2), with the associated Figure A3-I, Table A2-1 and 3∙10^-1 values applying.

For the S2 (variable) signal, the luminous intensity shall meet the minimum values in cd given in the table (6.0∙10^1, 7.30∙10^2 and 3.65∙10^2), with the associated Figure A3-I and Table A2-1 applying, and the minimum value of 3∙10^-1 for day and 7∙10^-2 for night.

For the S3 (steady) signal, the luminous intensity shall meet the minimum values in cd given in the table (2.5∙10^1, 1.10∙10^2 and 5.5∙10^1), with the associated Figure A3-III and Table A2-1 applying, and the 3∙10^-1 value.

For the S4 (variable) signal, the luminous intensity shall meet the minimum values in cd given in the table (2.5∙10^1, 1.60∙10^2 and 8.0∙10^1), with the associated Figure A3-III and Table A2-1 applying, and the minimum value of 3∙10^-1 for day and 7∙10^-2 for night.

For the MS (steady) signal, the luminous intensity shall meet the minimum values in cd given in the table (4.0∙10^1, 2.60∙10^2 and 1.30∙10^2), with the associated Figure A3-I and Table A2-1 applying, and the 3∙10^-1 value.
The minimum luminous intensity of the stop lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall comply with the values specified in Table 7.

For a category S3 or S4 stop lamp intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, the colorimetric characteristics shall be verified with the worst-case combination(s) of lamp and rear window(s) or sample plate(s).
For the stop lamps pair (MS), the standard light distribution may be considered, at the request of the applicant, from the VV line to the outboard only.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two reversing lamp samples supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 10.
Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied at the 30° inwards verification angle.
The pair-only installation condition shall be clearly explained in the application for approval and relating documents (see paragraph 3.1.).
Where type approval is granted applying the pair-only condition, paragraph 9.1.3. of the communication form (see Annex 1) shall state that the device shall only be installed in a pair.

For the AR entry of the geometric visibility angle table, the minimum luminous intensity in cd shall be 8.0∙10^1, 3.00∙10^2, 6.00∙10^2 and 8.00∙10^3 across the angle ranges given in the table columns (in or above the h-plane; below the h-plane down to 5°D; below 5°D).
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.

The F1 (steady) signal shall meet the minimum luminous intensities of 1.50∙10^2 cd and 3.00∙10^2 cd listed in the table for the angles of geometric visibility, with the definition given in Figure A3-VI.

The F2 (variable) signal shall meet the minimum luminous intensities of 1.50∙10^2 cd and 8.40∙10^2 cd listed in the table for the angles of geometric visibility, with the definition given in Figure A3-VI.
Lamps shall be manufactured so as to conform to the type approved under UN R148.
Compliance with the requirements set forth in paragraph 5. of UN R148 shall be verified by the procedure that follows.
The minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 4 shall be complied with.
The minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 5 shall be complied with during conformity of production checks.
No measured value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.
For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12.

For a daytime running lamp intended for installation on category L3 vehicles, whose designed maximum luminous intensity does not exceed 7.00∙10² cd as identified in Annex 1, 7.00∙10² cd shall be applied as the maximum luminous intensity for the conformity of production procedures set forth in Annexes 4 and 5.
For rear-registration plate illuminating lamps, the unfavourable deviation with respect to the gradient of luminance shall be as shown in Table 13.
For rear-registration plate illuminating lamps, the unfavourable deviation with respect to the gradient of luminance shall be 2.5 x Bo/cm, comparable to 20 per cent.
For rear-registration plate illuminating lamps, the unfavourable deviation with respect to the gradient of luminance shall be 3.0 x Bo/cm, comparable to 30 per cent.
The authority which has granted the type approval may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility.
The normal frequency of verifications by the type-approval authority of the conformity control methods applied in each production facility shall be once every two years.

Where doubt exists about compliance of non-replaceable filament light sources with lifetime requirements and/or, for colour coated filament light sources, with colour endurance requirements (as specified in paragraph 4.11 of IEC 60809, Edition 4), conformity shall be checked as specified in paragraph 4.11 of IEC 60809, Edition 4.

To verify that a preceding-series UN type-approval remains acceptable, the change index applicable to the pertinent lamp (function) shall not differ from its change index as indicated in the latest series of amendments to UN R148.
A reversing lamp shall be installed on a vehicle only as part of a pair of reversing lamps.
The maximum mounting height of a manoeuvring lamp is a required characteristic to be stated in the approval documentation; no numerical value is given in this paragraph.
The daytime running lamp shall be intended exclusively for installation on vehicles of category L3.
The designed maximum luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp shall not exceed 7.00∙102 cd.
When the daytime running lamp is reduced, its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 1.4∙102 cd.
The manufacturer shall indicate (yes/no) whether the luminous intensity of the reversing projector is reduced to not exceed 8.00∙10^3 cd.
The list of documents deposited with the Type Approval Authority that has granted approval shall be annexed to the approval communication.
The list of documents deposited with the Type Approval Authority may be obtained on request.
A singular stop lamp (MS) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 45° inboard and 45° outboard, and a minimum vertical angle of 15° above and 10° below.
A stop lamp pair (MS) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 0° inboard and 45° outboard, and a minimum vertical angle of 15° above and 10° below.
A front/rear parking lamp (77R) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 0° inboard and 45° outboard, and a minimum vertical angle of 15° above and 15° below.
A daytime running lamp (RL) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 20° inboard and 20° outboard, and a minimum vertical angle of 10° above and 5° below.
A high mounted stop lamp (S3, S4) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 10° inboard and 10° outboard, and a minimum vertical angle of 10° above and 5° below.
A side direction indicator (5) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 5° in direction A and 55° in direction B, and a minimum vertical angle of 15° above and 15° below.
A side parking lamp shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 0° and 45° measured for front and rear, and a minimum vertical angle of 15° above and 15° below.
A side marker lamp (SM1) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 45° in direction A and 45° in direction B, and a minimum vertical angle of 10° above and 10° below.
A side marker lamp (SM2) shall provide a minimum horizontal angle of 30° in direction A and 30° in direction B, and a minimum vertical angle of 10° above and 10° below.

The angles shown (the photometric angles that take account of partial occultation by the rear registration plate illuminating lamp) must be adhered to in the directions in which there is most occultation.
The rear registration plate illuminating lamp must be designed so that the areas partly occulted are reduced to the minimum strictly necessary.
The minimum intensity percentages given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

For front and rear direction indicator lamps, front and rear position lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, parking lamps, stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS, and side marker lamps installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light pattern of the lamp should be substantially uniform.

For each part of the grid field formed by the grid lines, the light intensity in each direction within that part shall be at least the lowest minimum value shown (as a percentage) on the grid lines surrounding that direction.

For reversing lamps, where visual examination appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, a check shall be made to ensure that no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement is below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for those directions.

For the standard light distribution of daytime running lamps, the minimum luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage of the minimum intensity required by Table 6 that is shown in the values of the figure.
For direction indicator lamps of category 6, the luminous intensity at the reference direction H = 5°, V = 0° shall correspond to the minimum value prescribed in Table 8.

For direction indicator lamps of category 6, the minimum luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be the percentage of the minimum required intensity (Table 8) given by the values shown in the standard light distribution.
For each direction of measurement, the light intensity of the reversing lamp shall be at least the minimum intensity (in cd) given by the values shown in figure A3-V.
On the vehicle, the reference axes (H = 0° and V = 0°) shall be horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, and oriented in the required direction of visibility.
The reference axes (H = 0° and V = 0°) shall pass through the centre of reference of the reversing lamp.
If visual examination of a rear fog lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, a check shall be made.
For a rear fog lamp, outside the axes, no intensity measured within the rhombus defined by the extreme directions of measurement shall be below 7.5∙10^1 cd.

For devices illuminating two or all of the plates, the measurement points used shall be obtained by combining the corresponding plate drawings (Figure A3-XIII) in accordance with the outline indicated by the make or manufacturer.
When two measurement points are less than 30 mm apart, only one of those measurement points shall be used.

The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint only if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R148.

With respect to photometric performances, the conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested when testing photometric performances of any lamp chosen at random according to paragraph 4.8. of UN R148.
For a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, if the results of the test described above do not meet the requirements, the tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148.
The holder of the type approval shall demonstrate the use of the non-replaceable filament light source(s) in normal production.
The holder of the type approval shall show the identification of the non-replaceable filament light source(s) as indicated in the type approval documentation.
For each type of lamp, the holder of the type approval shall carry out at least the following tests, at appropriate intervals, as verification of conformity by the manufacturer.
The tests carried out by the holder of the type approval for verification of conformity shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.
If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested.
The manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
Tests of conformity under UN R148 shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in UN R148.
In any conformity test carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used only with the consent of the competent authority responsible for approval tests.
The manufacturer shall prove that the applied test methods are equivalent to those laid down in UN R148.
In all cases, the reference methods used shall be those specified in UN R148, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
Samples of lamps shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch.
The assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories.
A manufacturer may group together records concerning the same type from several factories, provided these factories operate under the same quality system and quality management.
The sampled lamp shall be subjected to photometric measurements for the minimum values at the points listed in Annex 3.
The sampled lamp shall be subjected to colorimetric measurement of the required chromaticity coordinates.
The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results.

The manufacturer shall define, in agreement with the competent authority, criteria governing the acceptability of its products in order to meet the requirements for verification of conformity of products in paragraph 6.1. of this Regulation.
The acceptability criteria shall be such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 5 is 0.95.

The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, only if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

With respect to photometric performance, the conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of any lamp chosen at random, no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.

If a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source does not meet the requirements in the photometric performance test described above, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with (the applicable chromaticity requirements) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent.
The measurement may be terminated if the deviation of both lamps of sample A is not more than 0 per cent.
The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of sample A or sample B is more than 20 per cent.
The manufacturer shall be requested to bring its production in line with the requirements (alignment).
A repeated sampling according to paragraph 3 shall be carried out within two months after the notification.
Samples A and B shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire CoP process is finished.
The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested only if the deviation of any specimen of samples C and D (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent.
The measurement may be terminated when the deviation of both lamps of sample C is not more than 0 per cent.
The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of sample C or D is of the kind listed in the enumeration that follows this paragraph.

The manufacturer shall be requested again to bring its production in line with the requirements (alignment) when the deviation of all specimens of the samples is more than 20 per cent but not more than 30 per cent.
A second repeated sampling according to paragraph 4 shall be carried out within two months after the notification.
The samples C and D shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire COP process is finished.
If one specimen of sample C or D is more than 30 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn.
If one specimen of sample C or D is more than 30 per cent, paragraph 5 of Annex 5 shall be applied.
The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples E and F (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent.
The measurement may be terminated if the deviation of both lamps of sample E is not more than 0 per cent.
The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent.
If the conformity of mass-produced lamps is contested under this paragraph (deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F more than 20 per cent), the approval shall be withdrawn.
If the conformity of mass-produced lamps is contested under this paragraph (deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F more than 20 per cent), paragraph 5 shall be applied.
When required under paragraphs 4.1. and 4.2. of Annex 5, approval of UN R148 shall be withdrawn according to paragraph 3.6. of UN R148.
The lamp shall be subjected to a one-hour test of continuous operation, following a 20-minute warm-up period.
The ambient temperature during the lamp test shall be 23 °C ± 5 °C.
The light source used in the lamp test shall be a light source of the category specified for the lamp.
The light source shall be supplied with a current at a voltage such that it gives the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources (filament light sources and other), the test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with paragraph 5.4.5. of this Regulation.
Where only the maximum power is specified, the test shall be carried out by regulating the voltage to obtain a power equal to 90 per cent of the specified power.
The specified average or maximum power referred to in this annex shall in all cases be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which that power reaches its highest value.
For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the test conditions set in paragraph 5.4.5. or 5.9.5. of this Regulation shall be applied.

Where light sources are operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity, the test shall be carried out under the conditions given at minimum 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity.
After the lamp has been stabilized at the ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the lamp shall be perceptible.
In case of doubt, the intensity of light shall be measured according to the paragraph referenced here (the reference is incomplete in the source text).
At the measurement referred to in this paragraph, the measured values shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.
For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured after photometric stability has occurred, by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 minute, after 10 minutes, and after photometric stability has occurred.

For all other lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
Direction indicator lamps shall be operated in flashing mode (f = 1.5 Hz, duty factor 50 per cent).

The luminous intensity distribution after 1 min of operation may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution either after 30 min of operation or after photometric stabilization, by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 min and either after 30 min of operation or after photometric stabilization.

Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the lamp shall additionally be checked for compliance, in addition to paragraph 1, at the point in time after switch ON listed for that lamp (function) in Table A8-1.

The luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying, at each test point, the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
The manufacturer shall fix the distribution of the technically permissible maximum mass between the axles in accordance with the method described in Annex 5.

For lighting devices for the rear registration plate and direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6, the light-emitting surface shall be used as the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
When a functional unit is used for the bending mode, its light distribution may vary as a function of the T-signal (turn-radius).
The light distribution of a functional unit shall be identical for a given T-signal (turn-radius) in all modes or classes in which it is used.
An LED module shall contain only LEDs as its light sources.
An LED module may optionally contain one or more holders for approved replaceable light sources.
The light emitting surface of a lighting device, light-signalling device or retro-reflector shall be declared in the request for approval according to one of the following conditions (a) or (b).
Where the outer lens is textured, the declared light emitting surface shall be all or part of the exterior surface of the outer lens.
Where the outer lens is non-textured, the outer lens may be disregarded when declaring the light emitting surface.
Where the outer lens is non-textured, the light emitting surface shall be as declared on the drawing in Annex 3.
If the lighting device has no reflector, the definition of paragraph 2.10.3.2. shall be applied.
If the reflector and lens are adjustable relative to one another, the mean adjustment should be used.

To determine the lower, upper and lateral limits of the illuminating surface of a light-signalling device, only screens with horizontal or vertical edges shall be used to verify the distance to the extreme edges of the vehicle and the height above the ground.
For other applications of the illuminating surface of a light-signalling device, e.g. distance between two lamps or functions, the shape of the periphery of this illuminating surface shall be used.
When measuring the illuminating surface of a light-signalling device, the screens shall remain parallel to each other.
Screen orientations other than parallel to each other (i.e. other than the orientations specified for the screens) may be used when measuring the illuminating surface.

In the case of a light-signalling device whose illuminating surface encloses either totally or partially the illuminating surface of another function or encloses a non-lighted surface, the illuminating surface may be considered to be the light emitting surface itself (see e.g. Annex 3, Parts 2, 3, 5 and 6).
When determining the lower, upper and lateral edges of the retro-reflector device, only horizontal and vertical planes shall be considered.

For a light-signalling device producing variable luminous intensities, its apparent surface, which may be variable as specified in paragraph 2.9.3., shall be considered under all conditions permitted by the variable intensity control, if applicable.

The application for approval of a vehicle type with regard to the installation of its lighting and light-signalling devices shall be submitted by the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative.
The application for approval shall be accompanied by the following documents and particulars, submitted in triplicate.
The application for approval shall be accompanied by a description of the vehicle type with regard to the items mentioned in paragraphs 2.2.1.1. to 2.2.1.4. of this Regulation.
The application for approval shall be accompanied by the restrictions on loading, particularly the maximum permissible load in the boot.
The application shall be accompanied by a list of the devices prescribed by the manufacturer for the lighting and light-signalling assembly.
The list of devices may include several types of device for each operation.
Each type of device listed shall be duly identified (component, type-approval mark, name of manufacturer, etc.).
The list of devices may include, in respect of each function, the additional annotation "or equivalent devices".
The application for approval shall be accompanied by a statement of the method used for the definition of the apparent surface (see paragraph 2.10.4.).
The method used to determine the apparent surface shall be declared for each lamp, as defined in paragraph 2.5.
The method used to determine the apparent surface for each lamp shall be recorded in item 10.2. of Annex 1.

Where an AFS is fitted on the vehicle, the applicant shall submit a detailed description of the AFS, as part of the application for approval, providing the information listed in the following sub-paragraphs.

At the manufacturer's discretion, the application may include a statement indicating whether lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light sources are allowed to be installed on the vehicle or not and, if this is allowed, which lamps.
Where a system is able to provide driver assistance projections on the road, the manufacturer shall provide a list of the patterns and symbols as part of the application documents.

An unladen vehicle fitted with a complete set of lighting and light-signalling equipment as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.2., and representative of the vehicle type to be approved, shall be submitted to the Technical Service responsible for conducting approval tests.
The document provided in Annex 1 to UN R48 shall be attached to the type-approval documentation.

If the vehicle type submitted for approval under this Regulation meets the requirements of the Regulation in respect of all the devices specified in the list, approval of that vehicle type shall be granted.
An approval number shall be assigned to each vehicle type approved.

The first two digits of the approval number shall indicate the series of amendments incorporating the most recent major technical amendments made to the Regulation at the time of issue of the approval (at present 08, corresponding to the 08 series of amendments).
The same Contracting Party shall not assign an approval number to another vehicle type, subject to the provisions of paragraph 7. of this Regulation.

The same Contracting Party shall not assign an approval number to the same vehicle type submitted with equipment not specified in the list referred to in paragraph 3.2.2, subject to the provisions of paragraph 7. of this Regulation.

Notice of approval, of extension or refusal of approval, or of production definitively discontinued, for a vehicle type/part under this Regulation shall be communicated to the Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation by means of a form conforming to the model in Annex 1 to this Regulation.
Every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under UN R48 shall have an international approval mark affixed conspicuously, in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form.

Where the approval symbol need not be repeated, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols of all the Regulations under which approval has been granted in the country that granted approval under UN R48 shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible.
The approval mark shall be indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate affixed by the manufacturer.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that, under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be fitted so that it is not possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
The illuminating lamps described in paragraphs 2.5.1., 2.5.2. and 2.5.10. shall be installed so that correct adjustment of their orientation can easily be carried out.

For headlamps fitted with measures to prevent discomfort to other road-users in a country where traffic operates on the side of the road opposite to that of the country for which the headlamp was designed, such measures shall be achieved automatically or by the vehicle user with the vehicle in the park condition, without the need for special tools other than those provided with the vehicle.
The vehicle manufacturer shall provide detailed instructions with the vehicle for achieving the anti-discomfort measures on headlamps fitted with them.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road.
For side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.

For all signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
A tolerance of ±3° in each direction shall be allowed on the orientation of the reference axis of light-signalling devices relative to the specified planes.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, where an AFS is installed, with the AFS in its neutral state.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
The requirement that lamps constituting a pair have substantially identical photometric characteristics shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the above requirements of paragraph 5 shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another.

Where lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, shall be fulfilled.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) that can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.
Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps shall not be reciprocally incorporated with each other.
Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, the following conditions shall be met (conditions are specified in the subsequent sub-paragraphs of 5.7.1.3, not in this paragraph).

Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.

A single lamp (as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a)) whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts shall be installed so that the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis, occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

A single lamp (as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a)) whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts shall be installed so that the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis, does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
The installation requirements for single lamps with a multi-part apparent surface do not apply to a single retro-reflector.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed such that the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed such that the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system.
A lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.
Two lamps, or an even number of lamps forming a band or strip, shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
The band or strip of lamps shall extend on both sides of the vehicle to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The band or strip of lamps shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
The illumination of a band or strip lamp surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends of the surface.
The light-emitting surface of a band or strip lamp may be constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements.

Where the light-emitting surface is constituted by juxtaposed elements, the individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
The maximum height above the ground shall be measured from the highest point of the apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis.
The minimum height above the ground shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis.
Where the maximum and minimum height above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
For the purpose of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the height position of a lamp above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
For a dipped-beam headlamp, the minimum height above the ground shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, independent of its utilization.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Direction-indicator lamps shall be flashing lamps.
The vehicle-hazard warning signal shall be a flashing lamp signal.
Amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7 shall be flashing lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be a flashing lamp signal.
The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light.
The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF.
The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function.
Any variation in the photometric characteristics of a lamp permitted under 5.9.2 shall comply with the technical provisions for that lamp.

The photometric characteristics of a direction indicator lamp of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b may be varied during a flash by sequential activation of light sources as specified in paragraph 5.6. of UN Regulation No. 6 or paragraph 5.6.11. of UN Regulation No. [LSD].

The variation of photometric characteristics during a flash permitted in paragraph 5.9.3. shall not apply when direction indicator lamps of categories 2a and 2b are operated as emergency stop signal according to paragraph 6.23.1. of this Regulation.
The answer-back signal may flash and/or vary in luminous intensity and/or vary in apparent surface.
The lamp(s) used for answer-back signal shall operate according to the conditions specified in the general specifications and/or in dedicated paragraph 6.27.
The reversing projection may vary according to the steering wheel angle, the speed of the vehicle, and/or the proximity to an obstacle.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.
Lighting devices fitted for the interior lighting of the vehicle shall not be taken into account when assessing light that could give rise to confusion.
Reversing projections shall not be taken into account when assessing light that could give rise to confusion.

For red light visible towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp when viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

For white light towards the rear of a vehicle, excluding reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, the apparent surface of a white lamp shall not be directly visible to an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement above (no red light emitted to the front and no white light emitted to the rear that could give rise to confusion) shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if fitted), the side-marker lamps (if fitted), and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
