The electrical connections shall be such that the main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps cannot be switched ON unless the lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11 are also switched ON.

The interlock requirement in paragraph 5.12 does not apply to main-beam or dipped-beam headlamps when their luminous warnings consist of intermittent lighting up at short intervals of the main-beam headlamp, intermittent lighting up at short intervals of the dipped-beam headlamp, or alternate lighting up at short intervals of the main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps.

The dipped-beam headlamps and/or the main-beam headlamps and/or the front fog lamps may substitute the function of the front position lamps, provided that the conditions listed in the following sub-paragraphs are met.
The substituting lamp/function shall meet, for the respective position lamp, the geometric visibility requirements prescribed for front position lamps in paragraph 6.9.5.
The substituting lamp/function shall meet, for the respective position lamp, the minimum photometric values according to the angles of light distribution.
Where UN R48 prescribes a closed-circuit tell-tale, that tell-tale may be replaced by an "operating" tell-tale.
Concealment of lamps shall be prohibited.
Main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps may be concealed when they are not in use.
In the event of any failure affecting the operation of the concealment device(s), the concealable lamps that are already in use shall remain in the position of use.

In the event of any failure affecting the operation of the concealment device(s), the concealable lamps that are not already in use shall be capable of being moved into the position of use without the aid of tools.
It shall be possible to move the concealable lamps into the position of use and switch them ON by means of a single control.
The single control shall not exclude the possibility of moving the concealable lamps into the position of use without switching them ON.
For grouped main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps, the single control shall be required only to activate the dipped-beam headlamps.
It shall not be possible deliberately, from the driver's seat, to stop the movement of switched ON concealable lamps before they reach their position of use.
If there is a danger of dazzling other road users by the movement of the concealable lamps, the lamps may light up only when they have reached their position of use.
When the concealment device has a temperature of -30 °C to +50 °C, the headlamps shall be capable of reaching the position of use within three seconds of initial operation of the control.
The light emitted by the main-beam headlamp shall be white.
The light emitted by the dipped-beam headlamp shall be white.
The light emitted by the front fog lamp shall be white or selective yellow.
The light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The light emitted by the direction-indicator lamp shall be amber.
The light emitted by the hazard warning signal shall be amber.
The light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by the emergency stop signal shall be amber or red.
The light emitted by the rear-end collision alert signal shall be amber.
The light emitted by the rear registration plate lamp shall be white.
The light emitted by the front position lamp shall be white.
The light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by the rear fog lamp shall be red.

The light emitted by the parking lamp shall be white at the front and red at the rear; it shall be amber if the parking lamp is reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.

The light emitted by the side-marker lamp shall be amber, except that the rearmost side-marker lamp may be red if it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, rear end-outline marker lamp, rear fog lamp or stop lamp, or is grouped or has part of its light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The light emitted by the end-outline marker lamp shall be white at the front and red at the rear.
The light emitted by the daytime running lamp shall be white.
The light returned by the non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.
The light returned by the triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.
The light returned by the non-triangular front retro-reflector shall be identical to the incident light.

The light returned by the non-triangular side retro-reflector shall be amber, except that the rearmost side retro-reflector may be red if it is grouped or has part of its light emitting surface in common with the rear position lamp, rear end outline marker lamp, rear fog lamp, stop lamp, red rearmost side-marker lamp or non-triangular rear retro-reflector.
The light emitted by the cornering lamp shall be white.
The light emitted by conspicuity markings shall be white to the front, white or yellow to the side, and red or yellow to the rear.
The light emitted by the adaptive front-lighting systems (AFS) shall be white.
The light emitted by the exterior courtesy lamp shall be white.
The exterior courtesy lamp shall additionally comply with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the exterior courtesy lamp.
The light emitted by the manoeuvring lamp shall be white.
The answer-back signal shall comply with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The light emitted by the reversing projection shall be white.
Contracting Parties applying this Regulation may allow the use of white conspicuity markings to the rear in their territories.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
Any lamp may be installed on movable components only if the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors, both triangular and non-triangular, may be installed only on movable components (the permitted conditions are listed in the enumeration that follows this paragraph).
Additional lamps for the rear position, rear direction-indicator and rear triangular retro-reflector functions may be switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position.

Additional lamps that are switched ON while the movable component is in a fixed open position shall satisfy all position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
Where the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system, one of the following conditions (a) or (b) shall apply.
Where the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1. shall be satisfied.

Additional lamps for the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. may be switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, provided they satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

Where the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component (excluding direction indicator lamps), the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

The inwards geometric visibility requirement(s) for the interdependent lamp(s) in condition (b) are deemed satisfied only if those lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

For direction indicator lamps in an interdependent lamp system partly on a fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, geometric visibility, photometric and colorimetric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

The requirement for direction indicator lamps to meet all position, geometric visibility, photometric and colorimetric requirements at all fixed positions does not apply where additional lamps are switched ON, when the movable component is in any fixed open position, to fulfil or complete the geometric visibility angle, provided those additional lamps satisfy all the position, photometric and colorimetric requirements applicable to direction indicator lamps installed on the movable component.
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on the movable components shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and that component is in its normal position(s) of use, the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with UN R48.
A lamp installed on a movable component in its normal position(s) of use shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with UN R48.

For dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps, the return-to-position requirement is satisfied only if, after 10 moves of the movable components and returns to the normal position, no measured angular inclination of the lamp relative to its support differs by more than 0.15 per cent from the average of the 10 measured values.

If the 0.15 per cent deviation is exceeded, each limit specified in paragraph 6.2.6.1.1. shall be modified by this excess so as to decrease the allowed range of inclinations when checking the vehicle according to Annex 6 of UN R48.

The apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis, of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, by more than 50 per cent in any fixed position different from the normal position of use.

Additional lamps that satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the above indicated front and rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

A remark in the communication form (item 10.1 of Annex 1) shall inform other Administrations that more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components.

A notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road, for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.

Lamps approved with light sources according to UN Regulation No. 37 shall be fitted in the vehicle so that the light source can be correctly replaced without expert assistance and without special tools other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer, unless the light sources are non-replaceable light sources as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2.
The vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the light source replacement procedure.
Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, that light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

A temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed only if the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
The replacement device used for a temporary fail-safe replacement of a rear position lamp's light-signalling function shall remain operational in its original safety function.

During replacement of a rear position lamp's light-signalling function, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate the occurrence of a temporary replacement and the need for repair.
Where an AFS is fitted, the AFS shall be considered equivalent to a pair of dipped-beam headlamps.
Where an AFS provides main-beam function(s), the AFS shall be considered equivalent to a pair of main-beam headlamps.

Rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 may have variable luminous intensity control, responding simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., only if the conditions in (a) and (b) are met.

When the lamps with variable luminous intensity control (category 2b, R2 and S2) are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, their intensities shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
Across the entire intensity range, where a specific ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps is prescribed, that ratio shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

The luminous intensity of the rear direction indicator lamp, rear position lamp or stop lamp may be increased or decreased, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, in relation to the following conditions: (a) ambient lighting, (b) fog, (c) snowfall, (d) rain, (e) spray, (f) dust clouds, (g) contamination of the light emitting surface.

Independently of the environmental conditions in 5.26.1, a decrease of the luminous intensity of the lamps, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed when the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal to or less than 20 m.
Once a luminous intensity decrease has been activated, it may remain active as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 50 km/h.
Stop lamps of category S4 and rear fog lamps of category F2 may produce variable luminous intensity based on the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1 and 5.26.2.
Stop lamps of category S4 and rear fog lamps of category F2 may produce variable luminous intensity independently from the other lamps.
During transition between luminous intensity levels of the functions in this section, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed.
It may be possible for the driver to set the functions above (the rear direction indicator, rear position and stop functions with variable intensity) to static luminous intensities.

For vehicles of M and N categories, the applicant shall demonstrate to the Technical Service responsible for type approval testing that the electric power supply conditions for the devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., and 2.5.4. are met. (Source paragraph is truncated after '2.5.4.,'; the remaining device references and the specified condition are not included in the provided text.)

For devices that, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested using a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode, or at a voltage requested by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of those devices shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as approved.

In all electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.

The provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1 and 5.27.2 shall not apply to devices which include: an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
For vehicles of M and N categories, the applicant shall attach to the approval documentation a report describing the methods used to demonstrate compliance and the results obtained.
There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity.
Obstacles within the angles of geometric visibility are not taken into account only if they were already present when the lamp was type-approved.
When measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to the original direction so as to achieve the same measurement accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal is reduced to 5º (lamp mounted less than 750 mm above the ground, measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5º below the horizontal.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all of its interdependent lamps are operated together.
Where applicable, each lamp (device) installed on a vehicle shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulation specified in the relevant subparagraph of paragraph 6 of UN R48.
A light-signalling lamp incorporating a manufacturer logo shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

A lamp installed on a vehicle approved under UN R48 and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories under Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted only with light sources approved according to those light source categories.
The light intensity of an external status indicator for VAS, AS or immobilizer shall not exceed 0.5 cd in any direction.
The colour of the light emitted by an external status indicator for VAS, AS or immobilizer shall be white, red or amber.
The area of the apparent surface of an external status indicator for VAS, AS or immobilizer shall not be larger than 20 cm2.
Up to two external status indicators for VAS, AS and immobiliser may be fitted on a vehicle.
When up to two external status indicators for VAS, AS and immobiliser are fitted on a vehicle, the apparent surface of each indicator shall not exceed 10 cm2.

A device type approved under any preceding series of amendments to UN Regulations Nos. 148, 149 and/or 150 is deemed equivalent to a device type approved under the latest series of amendments to the pertinent UN Regulations, only when the change indexes (as defined in paragraph 2.1.6.) related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ.
A device type deemed equivalent under paragraph 5.33. may be fitted on the vehicle to be type approved without updating the device type approval documents and device markings.
Lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) may be used only in the case where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive.

To verify that the statement in paragraph 3.2.8. is respected, both at type approval and in the conformity of production verification, the presence of the marking on the lamps related to the use of LED substitute light source(s) shall be checked.
The Driver Assistance Projection shall be constituted of patterns, symbols or both.

Driver Assistance Projection symbols and patterns shall relate to, and be limited only to, warning/highlighting of: (a) the presence of a hazardous traffic situation; (b) the presence of other road users which require the driver's attention; (c) maintaining the distances to surrounding road users and infrastructure; (d) maintaining the correct lane.
The patterns and symbols of the Driver Assistance Projection shall be explained in the owner's handbook.
Only the symbols and patterns listed in Annex 16 (together with their associated underlying conditions) may be used for the Driver Assistance Projection.
Flashing of Driver Assistance Projection shall not be permitted, unless expressly allowed for the use cases described under the conditions in Annex 16.
Transforming of Driver Assistance Projection shall not be permitted, unless expressly allowed for the use cases described under the conditions in Annex 16.
It shall always be possible to manually deactivate and reactivate the system which operates the Driver Assistant Projection.
Projected symbols and patterns shall no longer be projected when their associated underlying conditions allowing them to be shown do not exist anymore.
Projected symbols and patterns shall stop flashing when their associated underlying conditions allowing them to flash no longer exist.

The Driver Assistance Projection shall be deactivated automatically in case of an electrically detectable failure of the system that affects the visual information on the road given by the Driver Assistance Projection.
The Driver Assistance Projection shall not interfere with information displayed by the Field of Vision Assistant as defined in UN Regulation No. 125.
The Driver Assistance Projection shall not be switched ON when the windshield wiper is switched ON and its continuous operation has occurred for a period of at least two minutes.
Driver Assistance Projection, other than the wrong way warning, predicted trajectory and risk of collision warning, shall not be switched ON when the vehicle speed is below 65 km/h.
When Driver Assistance Projection is already switched ON, it may remain switched ON as long as the vehicle speed remains above 40 km/h.

Except for predicted trajectory, the lateral distance from the outer edges of the Driver Assistance Projection with respect to the longitudinal median plane or to the trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle shall not be more than 1,250 mm.
The Driver Assistance Projection may be adapted according to the predicted trajectory of the centre of gravity of the vehicle, when illustrating the predicted trajectory.
The Driver Assistance Projection shall not be wider than the width of the vehicle including any fitted accessories and, if applicable, the trailer.
In any case, the Driver Assistance Projection shall not be more than 2,600 mm.
The manufacturer shall demonstrate compliance with paragraphs 5.35.11. and 5.35.12.1. by calculation or by other means accepted by the Type Approval Authority.
The patterns used for the reversing projection shall be explained in the owner's handbook.
When reversing projection is provided, only the basic elements listed in Annex 17 shall be used.
When reversing projections are provided, the pattern of each reversing projection shall be constituted by one or more basic element(s) of the same type in a line.
The number, size, ratio and spacing between the basic elements in the reversing projection pattern are not restricted, provided that the requirements of paragraph 6.28.5. are met.
When more than one reversing projection is switched ON simultaneously, the projected patterns shall not overlap each other.

When the windshield wiper is switched ON and its continuous operation has occurred for a period of at least two minutes, each reversing projection whose luminous intensity exceeds 8.00∙10^3 cd shall either be switched OFF or have its luminous intensity reduced to a value less than or equal to 8.00∙10^3 cd.
Conformity to the requirement of paragraph 5.36.5 shall be verified at the time of the reversing projector type approval and indicated in the related communication form.
The applicant shall provide sufficient evidence that the reversing projection will not negatively affect rear camera system performance as defined in UN Regulation No. 158.
A reversing lamp shall be fitted on motor vehicles and on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4.
A reversing lamp may be fitted on trailers of category O1.
On motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm, one reversing lamp device shall be fitted.
On motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm, a second reversing lamp device may be fitted.
On vehicles with a length exceeding 6,000 mm, other than category M1 vehicles, two reversing lamp devices shall be fitted as mandatory.
On vehicles with a length exceeding 6,000 mm, other than category M1 vehicles, two further reversing lamp devices may be fitted as optional.
Reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be installed at a height of not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
For category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles, the maximum height of the reversing lamp above the ground may be increased to 1,400 mm.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle in the longitudinal (length) direction.

If installed, the two optional reversing lamp devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. may be fitted on the side of the vehicle, provided that the requirements of paragraphs 6.4.5.2. and 6.4.6.2. are fulfilled.

For the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2, if fitted on the side of the vehicle, geometric visibility is considered ensured only if the reference axis of the respective device is directed outwards with an angle β not exceeding 15° relative to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
For the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2, if fitted on the side of the vehicle, the vertical aim may be directed downwards.
If the two optional reversing lamps referred to in paragraph 6.4.2.2. are fitted on the side of the vehicle, the provisions of paragraph 6.4.5.2. shall apply.

The reversing lamp electrical connections shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position that makes operation of the propulsion system possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion-system start/stop control device is not in a position that makes operation of the propulsion system possible.

The electrical connections of the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. shall be such that these devices cannot be switched ON unless the reversing lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11. are switched ON.
The side-fitted devices may be switched ON for slow manoeuvres in forward motion of the vehicle up to a maximum vehicle speed of 15 km/h, provided that the conditions (a) to (c) are fulfilled.
The side-fitted devices shall be switched ON and OFF manually by a separate control.
If the side-fitted devices have been switched ON for slow manoeuvres, they may remain ON after reverse gear is disengaged.
The side-fitted devices shall be automatically switched OFF if the forward speed of the vehicle exceeds 15 km/h, regardless of the position of the separate control.
After the side-fitted devices have been automatically switched OFF due to forward speed exceeding 15 km/h, they shall remain switched OFF until deliberately being switched ON again.
A tell-tale for the reversing lamp is optional.
If the component regulation requires it, a tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp shall be provided.
The upward angle of 15° (above the horizontal) may be reduced to 5°.
Direction indicator lamps of category 6 shall have a visibility angle of 30° above and 5° below the horizontal.
The dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator shall not exceed 5°, as an upper limit where d ≤ 1.80 m (for M1 and N1 category vehicles, d ≤ 2.50 m).
For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
Stop lamp devices of category S1 or S2 shall be fitted on all categories of vehicles.
Stop lamp devices of category S3 or S4 shall be fitted on vehicles of category M1 and N1.
Stop lamp devices of category S3 or S4 shall not be mandatory on chassis-cabs or on N1 category vehicles with open cargo space.
Stop lamp devices of category S3 or S4 may be fitted on vehicle categories other than M1 and N1.
On all categories of vehicles, the stop lamp installation shall comprise two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device.

The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
On vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O2, O3 and O4, two optional category S1 or S2 stop lamp devices may be installed, except where a category S3 or S4 device is installed.

Only when the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle is not located on a fixed body panel but separates one or two movable parts of the vehicle (e.g. doors), and there is insufficient space to install a single S3 or S4 category device on the median longitudinal plane above such movable parts, two S3 or S4 category type "D" devices may be installed.

Only when the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle is not located on a fixed body panel but separates one or two movable parts of the vehicle (e.g. doors), and there is insufficient space to install a single S3 or S4 category device on the median longitudinal plane above such movable parts, one S3 or S4 category device may be installed offset to the left or to the right of the median longitudinal plane.

Only when the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle is not located on a fixed body panel but separates one or two movable parts of the vehicle (e.g. doors), and there is insufficient space to install a single S3 or S4 category device on the median longitudinal plane above such movable parts, an interdependent lamp system of category S3 or S4 may be installed.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the S1 or S2 stop lamp device whose apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, points outward shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of S1 or S2 stop lamp devices, in the direction of the reference axes, shall be not less than 600 mm.

For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of S1 or S2 stop lamp devices may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the centre of reference of an S3 or S4 stop lamp device shall be situated on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.

Where two S3 or S4 stop lamp devices are installed according to paragraph 6.7.2., they shall be positioned as close as possible to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, one on each side of that plane.

Where one S3 or S4 stop lamp offset from the median longitudinal plane is permitted according to paragraph 6.7.2., the offset, measured from the median longitudinal plane to the centre of reference of the lamp, shall not exceed 150 mm.
For S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices, the device shall be mounted above the ground at a height not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm.

For S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices, the height above the ground may be up to 2,100 mm only if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and the optional lamps are not installed.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements for the width and the symmetry of the lamps.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a vertical distance from the mandatory lamps as large as the shape of the bodywork makes possible.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be positioned not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

For S3 or S4 category stop lamp devices, the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface shall either be not more than 150 mm below the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the exposed surface of the glass or glazing of the rear window, or be not less than 850 mm above the ground.

The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of an S3 or S4 category stop lamp device shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices.
For S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices, the geometric visibility shall be provided at 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
For S1 and S2 stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
For S3 or S4 category stop lamp devices, the geometric visibility shall be provided at 10° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
For S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices, the geometric visibility shall be provided at 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where a stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
For S3 or S4 category devices, the angle shall be 10° above and 5° below the horizontal.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
A tell-tale for the stop lamp is optional.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp shall be fitted if the component regulation requires it.
The S3 or S4 category stop lamp device shall not be reciprocally incorporated with any other lamp.
An S3 or S4 category stop lamp device may be installed either outside or inside the vehicle.

Rear position lamp devices of category R, R1 or R2 are mandatory (shall be fitted).

In width, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For all vehicle categories other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm.
For vehicles other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
The height of the rear position lamp above the ground shall be not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm.
The height of the rear position lamp above the ground may be up to 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and the optional lamps are not installed.

If the optional rear position lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a vertical distance above the mandatory lamps as large as the shape of the bodywork makes possible.
If the optional rear position lamps are installed, they shall be placed not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
The rear position lamp's geometric visibility shall cover a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards.

The rear position lamp's geometric visibility shall cover a vertical angle of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.
Where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1. above), the 15° downward vertical visibility angle may be reduced to 5°.

The rear position lamp shall be visible through a horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards.
Where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward horizontal visibility angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The rear position lamp shall be visible through a vertical angle of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.
Where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward vertical visibility angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

A closed-circuit tell-tale shall be provided for the rear position lamp.
The rear position lamp closed-circuit tell-tale shall be combined with the tell-tale of the front position lamps.

Motor vehicles shall be fitted with a non-triangular rear retro-reflector.
Trailers may be fitted with a non-triangular rear retro-reflector, provided that it is grouped together with the other rear light-signalling devices.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials, including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4, may be fitted to the vehicle.
Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

In width, the point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be no more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For vehicle categories other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear retro-reflector, in the direction of the reference axes, shall be not less than 600 mm.
For vehicle categories other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
The rear retro-reflector, measured in height, shall be above the ground, not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm.
Where the rear retro-reflector is grouped with any rear lamp(s), its height above the ground shall not be more than 1,200 mm.

Where the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep the rear retro-reflector within 900 mm (or within 1,200 mm when grouped with rear lamp(s)), its height above the ground shall not be more than 1,500 mm.
Under the conditions set out in the preceding provision ("above"), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector (non-triangular) may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
A triangular rear retro-reflector shall be fitted on trailers.
A triangular rear retro-reflector shall not be fitted on motor vehicles.

The rear retro-reflector, triangular, shall be two retro-reflectors type-approved according to the requirements for Class IIIA or Class IIIB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials may be fitted only if they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
Two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.15.4 may be fitted as additional retro-reflecting devices.
For the rear retro-reflector, triangular, the apex of the triangle shall be directed upwards.

The point on the illuminating surface of the rear triangular retro-reflector that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The inner edges of the rear triangular retro-reflectors shall be not less than 600 mm apart.
The 600 mm minimum distance between the inner edges of the rear triangular retro-reflectors may be reduced to 400 mm only if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
The triangular rear retro-reflector shall be mounted above the ground, not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm in height.
Where the triangular rear retro-reflector is grouped with any rear lamp(s), its height above the ground shall not exceed 1,200 mm.

Where the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep the triangular rear retro-reflector within 900 mm (or within 1,200 mm when grouped with rear lamp(s)), its height above the ground shall not exceed 1,500 mm.
The triangular rear retro-reflector shall be geometrically visible through a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and 30° outwards.
The triangular rear retro-reflector shall be geometrically visible through a vertical angle of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.
Where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward vertical visibility angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The illuminating surface of the rear triangular retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
A front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be fitted on trailers.
A front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be fitted on motor vehicles having all forward facing lamps with reflectors concealable.
A front retro-reflector, non-triangular, may be fitted on motor vehicles other than those having all forward facing lamps with reflectors concealable.

The front retro-reflectors of a non-triangular front retro-reflector installation shall number two, each type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3.

As an alternative to the UN Regulation No. 3 approval, each of the two front retro-reflectors may be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials, including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.16.4., may be fitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
For vehicles other than trailers, the point on the illuminating surface farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
In the case of a trailer, the point of the illuminating surface farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be farther than 150 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
For all vehicle categories other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm.

For vehicles other than M1 and N1 whose overall width is less than 1,300 mm, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes may be reduced to 400 mm.
The front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mounted above the ground at a height of not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm.
The height of the front retro-reflector, non-triangular, above the ground may be up to 1,500 mm only if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep the height within 900 mm.
The front retro-reflector shall provide a visibility angle of 30° horizontally, both inwards and outwards.
For trailers, the inward horizontal visibility angle of the front retro-reflector may be reduced to 10°.
If, because of the construction of a trailer, the horizontal visibility angle cannot be met by the mandatory retro-reflectors, additional (supplementary) retro-reflectors shall be fitted.
