The additional (supplementary) retro-reflectors, in conjunction with the mandatory retro-reflectors, shall give the necessary horizontal visibility angle.
The front retro-reflector shall provide a visibility angle of 10° above and 10° below the horizontal.
Where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical visibility angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The illuminating surface of the front retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the front.
Side retro-reflectors (non-triangular) shall be fitted on all motor vehicles whose length exceeds 6 m.
Side retro-reflectors (non-triangular) shall be fitted on all trailers.
Side retro-reflectors (non-triangular) may be fitted on motor vehicles whose length does not exceed 6 m.
The number of side retro-reflectors shall be such that the requirements for longitudinal positioning are complied with.

Side retro-reflectors shall be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

The devices referred to in the truncated preceding clause (see paragraph 6.17.4. below) are permitted only if they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
The side retro-reflector shall be mounted above the ground at a height of not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm.
When the side retro-reflector is grouped with any lamp(s), its height above the ground shall not exceed 1,200 mm.

Where the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep the side retro-reflector within 900 mm or 1,200 mm (respectively, depending on whether it is grouped with lamps), or where the presence of the device is not mandatory according to paragraph 6.17.1., its height above the ground shall not exceed 1,500 mm.
At least one side retro-reflector shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle.
The foremost side retro-reflector shall be fitted not further than 3 m from the front of the vehicle, or not further than 4 m from the front for semi-trailers.
The distance between two adjacent side retro-reflectors shall not exceed 3 m; this does not apply to M1 and N1 category vehicles.

If the structure, design or operational use of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with the 3 m adjacent-spacing requirement, the distance between adjacent side retro-reflectors may be increased to 4 m.
The distance between the rearmost side retro-reflector and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m.
For motor vehicles whose length does not exceed 6 m, it is sufficient to have one side retro-reflector fitted within the first third and/or one within the last third of the vehicle length.

For M1 vehicles whose length exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m, it is sufficient to have one side retro-reflector fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.
The side retro-reflector shall meet the geometric visibility requirement of a horizontal angle of 45° to the front and to the rear.
The side retro-reflector shall meet the geometric visibility requirement of a vertical angle of 10° above and 10° below the horizontal.
Where a side retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical visibility angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The illuminating surface of the side retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other side lamp.

Full contour marking shall be fitted to the rear of vehicles exceeding 2,100 mm in width that are category N2 with a maximum mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes or category N3, excluding chassis-cabs, incomplete vehicles and tractors for semi-trailers.
Full contour marking shall be fitted to the rear of vehicles exceeding 2,100 mm in width that are category O3 or O4, excluding incomplete vehicles.

Vehicles exceeding 6,000 mm in length (including the drawbar for trailers) of category N2 with a maximum mass exceeding 7.5 tonnes, or of category N3, shall be fitted with partial contour marking to the side, except chassis-cabs, incomplete vehicles and tractors for semi-trailers.
Vehicles exceeding 6,000 mm in length (including the drawbar for trailers) of category O3 or O4 shall be fitted with partial contour marking to the side, except incomplete vehicles.

A line marking may be installed instead of the mandatory contour marking only if the shape, structure, design or operational requirements of the vehicle make it impossible to install the mandatory contour marking.
If the exterior surfaces of the bodywork are partially constituted of flexible material, the line marking shall be installed on rigid part(s) of the vehicle.
If the exterior surfaces of the bodywork are partially constituted of flexible material, the remaining portion of conspicuity markings may be fitted on the flexible material.
If the exterior surfaces of the bodywork are constituted fully of flexible material, the line marking may be fitted on the flexible material.

Where the manufacturer, after verification by the Technical Service, proves to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that it is impossible, due to operational requirements which may require a special shape, structure or design of the vehicle, to comply with the requirements contained in paragraphs (the cross-reference is truncated in the source text), the manufacturer must provide that proof.
Where a requirement in paragraphs 6.21.2. to 6.21.7.5. cannot be fully met, partial fulfilment of some of these requirements is acceptable.
Partial fulfilment of the conspicuity requirements shall be conditional upon meeting a portion of the requirements where possible.
The application of conspicuity markings that partially meet the requirements shall be maximised on the vehicle structure.

Where structure is available, additional brackets or plates containing material type-approved to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 104, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150, may be fitted to ensure clear and uniform signalling compatible with the objective of conspicuity.

Where partial fulfilment is acceptable, retro-reflective devices of Class IVA type-approved to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150, or brackets containing retro-reflecting material type-approved to the photometric requirements of Class C of the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 104, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150, may substitute part of the required conspicuity markings.
Where retro-reflective devices substitute part of the required conspicuity markings, at least one of these devices shall be installed per 1,500 mm.
The necessary information shall be indicated in the communication form.

Vehicles of all other categories not otherwise specified in paragraphs 6.21.1.1 and 6.21.1.2, including the cab of tractor units for semi-trailers and the cab of chassis-cabs, shall be fitted with conspicuity markings to the rear and to the side.
Partial or full contour marking may be applied instead of the mandatory line markings.
Full contour marking may be applied instead of the mandatory partial contour marking.
On vehicles of categories O2, O3 and O4, line marking shall be applied to the front.
Partial or full contour marking shall not be applied to the front of the vehicle.
Conspicuity markings shall be arranged as close as practicable to horizontal and vertical, compatible with the shape, structure, design and operational requirements of the vehicle.
If horizontal and vertical arrangement is not possible, fitted full or partial contour markings shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
Conspicuity markings shall be spaced as evenly as possible over the horizontal dimensions of the vehicle such that the total length and/or width of the vehicle can be identified.
The conspicuity marking shall be positioned as close as practicable to the edge of the vehicle.

The cumulative horizontal length of the conspicuity marking elements, as mounted on the vehicle, shall be at least 70 per cent of the overall width of the vehicle, excluding any horizontal overlap of individual elements.
The conspicuity marking shall be positioned as close as practicable to the ends of the vehicle.
The conspicuity marking shall reach to within 600 mm of each end of the vehicle.
For motor vehicles, the conspicuity marking shall be fitted at each end of the vehicle, or, for tractors for semi-trailers, at each end of the cab.

An alternative marking mode may be used within 2,400 mm from the front end of the motor vehicle, where a series of Class IVA or Class C retro-reflectors (type-approved to the specified UN Regulation No. 3, 150 or 104 amendment series) are mounted followed by the required conspicuity marking.
Each retro-reflector used in the alternative marking mode shall have a size of at least 25 cm2.
In the alternative marking mode, one retro-reflector shall be mounted not more than 600 mm from the front end of the vehicle.
In the alternative marking mode, additional retro-reflectors shall be spaced not more than 600 mm apart.
In the alternative marking mode, the distance between the last retro-reflector and the start of the conspicuity marking shall not exceed 600 mm.

The cumulative horizontal length of the conspicuity marking elements, as mounted on the vehicle, excluding any horizontal overlap of individual elements, shall be at least 70 per cent of the reference quantity that the paragraph introduces with a colon but does not state in this text.
The distance A between the foremost conspicuity marking and the front end of the vehicle shall not exceed 2,400 mm.
The lower element(s) of line markings and contour markings shall be mounted as low as practicable within the permitted height range.
The lower element(s) of line markings and contour markings shall be not less than 250 mm above the ground.
The lower element(s) of line markings and contour markings shall be not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.

A maximum mounting height of 2,500 mm for the lower element(s) of line markings and contour markings may be accepted where the shape, structure, design or operational conditions of the vehicle prevent compliance with the 1,500 mm maximum, or if necessary to fulfil the requirements of paragraphs 6.21.4.1.2. and 6.21.4.2.2., or the horizontal positioning of the line marking or the lower element(s) of the contour marking.
The necessary justification for installing conspicuity material higher than 1,500 mm shall be indicated in the communication form.

The conspicuity marking shall be considered visible if at least 70 per cent of the illuminating surface of the installed marking is visible when viewed by an observer positioned at any point within the observation planes defined below.

Side conspicuity markings shall be oriented as close as practicable to parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, compatible with the shape, structure, design and operation requirements of the vehicle.

If it is not possible to orient a side conspicuity marking parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, the marking shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.

To the rear and to the front of the vehicle, conspicuity markings shall be as close as practicable to parallel to the transverse plane of the vehicle, compatible with the shape, structure, design and operation requirements of the vehicle.

Where parallel orientation to the transverse plane of the vehicle is not possible, the rear and front conspicuity markings shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
Conspicuity markings are considered continuous only if the distance between adjacent elements is as small as possible and does not exceed 50 per cent of the shortest adjacent element length.

If the manufacturer proves to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that it is impossible to respect the 50 per cent value, the distance between adjacent elements of conspicuity markings may be larger than 50 per cent of the shortest adjacent element.
Where the 50 per cent distance limit is exceeded under the approved exception, the distance between adjacent conspicuity marking elements shall be as small as possible and shall not exceed 1,000 mm.
In the case of a partial contour marking, each upper corner shall be described by two lines at 90° to each other, each at least 250 mm in length.

If describing each upper corner by two lines at 90° each at least 250 mm long is not possible, the partial contour marking shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
The distance between the conspicuity marking fitted to the rear of a vehicle and each mandatory stop lamp should be greater than 200 mm.

Where rear marking plates type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 70, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150 are installed, the manufacturer may, at its discretion, consider these plates as part of the rear conspicuity marking when calculating the length of the conspicuity marking and its proximity to the side of the vehicle.
The locations on the vehicle designated for conspicuity markings shall allow for the installation of markings of at least 60 mm in width.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The answer-back signal shall be provided by approved lighting and light-signalling devices and exterior courtesy lamps.

Where the answer-back signal is provided by approved lighting and light-signalling devices and exterior courtesy lamps, the maximum luminous intensity per lamp shall not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line.
Front fog lamps, rear fog lamps and stop lamps shall not be used to provide the answer-back signal.

Every modification of the vehicle type, or of the installation of its lighting or light-signalling devices, or of the list referred to in paragraph 3.2.2. above, shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority which approved that vehicle type.

After being notified of a modification, the Type Approval Authority may then either take one of the alternative actions listed in the enumeration that follows this paragraph (the enumeration itself is not included in this paragraph).

The confirmation of extension or refusal of approval of the vehicle type, specifying the alteration, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 4.3 to the Parties to the Agreement applying UN R48.
The Type Approval Authority issuing the extension of approval shall assign a series number for that extension of approval.

The Type Approval Authority issuing the extension of approval shall inform the other Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation of the extension by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1 to this Regulation.
The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in Appendix 2 (E/ECE/324-E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.2) of the Agreement.
Any vehicle approved pursuant to UN R48 shall be manufactured so as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5 and 6 of that Regulation.

The holder of the approval shall ensure that, for each type of vehicle, at least the tests prescribed in Annex 9 to UN R48 or physical checks from which equivalent data may be derived are carried out.
The Type Approval Authority may carry out any test prescribed in this Regulation.
The conformity-of-production tests carried out by the Type Approval Authority shall be conducted on samples selected at random.
The Type Approval Authority shall not cause distortion of the manufacturer's delivery commitments when carrying out conformity-of-production tests.
The Type Approval Authority shall strive to obtain a conformity-of-production inspection frequency of once per year.

The Type Approval Authority may set the conformity-of-production inspection frequency at its discretion, based on its confidence in the arrangements for ensuring effective control of the conformity of production.
Where negative results are recorded, the Type Approval Authority shall ensure that all necessary steps are taken to re-establish the conformity of production as rapidly as possible.

The approval granted for a type of vehicle under UN R48 may be withdrawn if the requirements of the Regulation are not complied with, or if a vehicle bearing the approval mark does not conform to the approved type.

When a Contracting Party applying UN R48 withdraws an approval it has previously granted, it shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying UN R48 of the withdrawal by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1 to UN R48.
If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a type of vehicle approved in accordance with UN R48, the holder shall inform the authority which granted the approval.

Upon receiving the relevant communication of discontinued production, the approval authority shall inform the other Parties to the Agreement applying UN R48 by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1 to UN R48.

The Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying UN R48 shall communicate to the United Nations Secretary-General the names and addresses of the Technical Services responsible for conducting approval tests.

The Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying UN R48 shall communicate to the United Nations Secretary-General the names and addresses of the Type Approval Authorities which grant approval and to which forms certifying approval or extension or refusal or withdrawal of approval, issued in other countries, are to be sent.

Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall continue to recognize existing approvals under this Regulation that were granted before the date of mandatory application of the most recent series of amendment.

Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall not refuse to grant extensions of existing approvals granted before the date of mandatory application of the most recent series of amendment, except as indicated in paragraph 12.1.6.

When a vehicle type approved to any of the preceding series of amendments meets the requirements of UN R48 as amended by the most recent series of amendments, the Contracting Party which granted the approval shall notify the other Contracting Parties applying UN R48 of this.

The approval communication for the vehicle type shall state whether lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) are allowed to be installed on this vehicle type, by striking out whichever of 'yes' or 'no' does not apply.
If lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) are allowed on the vehicle type, the approval communication shall list the applicable lamps.

If the extent of coverage of the conspicuity marking is less than the minimum value of 70 per cent required by paragraphs 6.21.4.1.2. and 6.21.4.2.2. of the Regulation, comments regarding that extent of coverage shall be provided.
The approval mark in Model A (Annex 2, referenced by paragraph 4.4.) shall have dimension a of at least 8 mm.
The approval mark in Model B (Annex 2, referenced by paragraph 4.5.) shall have dimension a of at least 8 mm.
Component F1 shall not be transparent to component F2.

Where there are several points of contact between the vertical planes and the vehicle, the foremost point of contact shall correspond to the forward bounding plane and the rearmost point of contact shall correspond to the rearward bounding plane.
For the tests listed in this annex, the mass of the passengers shall be calculated on the basis of 75 kg per person.
The angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load conditions listed in the following paragraphs of Annex 5 2.1.1.

For the loading test, all seats of the vehicle shall be occupied and an evenly distributed load shall be placed in the luggage boot, so as to obtain the permissible load on the rear axle, or on the front axle if the boot is at the front.
If the vehicle has both a front boot and a rear boot, the additional load shall be appropriately distributed between the boots so as to obtain the permissible axle loads.

If the maximum permissible laden mass is reached before the permissible load on one of the axles, the loading of the boot(s) shall be limited to the figure that enables that maximum permissible laden mass to be reached.
For the test loading condition, the vehicle shall carry the driver plus an evenly distributed load in the boot, sufficient to obtain the permissible load on the corresponding axle.

If the maximum permissible laden mass is reached before the permissible load on the axle, the loading of the boot(s) shall be limited to the figure that enables that maximum permissible laden mass to be reached.
When determining the loading conditions, any loading restrictions laid down by the vehicle manufacturer shall be taken into account.
For vehicles in categories M2 and M3, the angle of the light beam from the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the loading conditions specified in the following list.

Vehicles shall be laden such that each axle carries its maximum technically permissible load, or until the maximum permissible mass of the vehicle is attained by loading the front and rear axles proportionally to their maximum technically permissible loads, whichever occurs first.
The angle of the light beam from the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the following loading conditions.

The vehicle shall be loaded with the driver plus a load distributed so as to give the maximum technically permissible load on the rear axle or axles, or the maximum permissible mass of the vehicle, whichever occurs first.
While loading the vehicle as specified, the front axle load shall not exceed the front axle load of the unladen vehicle plus 25 per cent of the maximum permissible payload on the front axle.

When the load platform is at the front, the front axle shall be considered in the same way as the rear axle in the loading condition above (i.e., it is the axle loaded to its maximum technically permissible load, subject to the front axle limit applying to the rear axle).

When a visual inspection of the dipped-beam pattern on the screen or a photometric method is used, the measurement shall be carried out in a dark environment (for example, a dark room) of sufficient area to allow the vehicle and the screen to be placed as shown in Figure 1.
The headlamp centres of reference shall be at a distance from the screen of at least 10 m.
The ground on which dipped-beam inclination measurements are made shall be as flat and horizontal as possible.
The reproducibility of dipped-beam inclination measurements shall be assured with an accuracy of ±0.5 mrad (±0.05 per cent inclination).

If a screen is used, its marking, position and orientation in relation to the ground and to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle shall be such that the reproducibility of the measurement of the dipped-beam inclination can be assured with an accuracy of ∀0.5 mrad (∀0.05 per cent inclination).
During measurements, the ambient temperature shall be between 10 and 30 °C.
Measurements shall be carried out on a vehicle that has travelled a distance of between 1,000 km and 10,000 km.
Measurements should preferably be carried out on a vehicle that has travelled a distance of 5,000 km.
Tyres shall be inflated to the full-load pressure specified by the vehicle manufacturer before the test.
The vehicle shall be fully replenished with fuel, water and oil before the test.
The vehicle shall be equipped with all the accessories and tools specified by the manufacturer before the test.
For full fuel replenishment, the fuel tank shall be filled to not less than 90 per cent of its capacity.
For the test, the vehicle shall have the parking brake released and the gearbox in neutral.
The vehicle shall be conditioned for at least 8 h at the temperature specified in paragraph 3.4. of this annex.
When a photometric or visual method is used, headlamps with a well-defined dipped-beam cut-off should preferably be installed on the vehicle under test to facilitate the measurements.
Other means may be used to obtain a more precise reading, for example removal of the headlamp lens.
The variation in either dipped-beam or vehicle inclination (depending on the method chosen) shall be measured separately for each side of the vehicle.
The results obtained from both the left and right headlamps under all load conditions specified in Annex 5 shall be within the limits set out in paragraph 5.5.
The load shall be applied gradually, without subjecting the vehicle to excessive shocks.
Where an AFS is fitted, the measurements shall be carried out with the AFS in its neutral state.
The vehicle shall be prepared as specified in paragraph 4 of this annex before the initial inclination is determined.
The vehicle shall be laden as specified in Annex 5 in the first loading condition of the respective vehicle category when the initial inclination is determined.
Before each measurement of the initial inclination, the vehicle shall be rocked as specified in paragraph 5.4 of this annex.
The initial inclination measurements shall be made three times.
If none of the three measured results differs by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination) from the arithmetic mean of the results, that arithmetic mean shall constitute the final result.
If any measurement differs from the arithmetic mean of the results by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination), a further series of 10 measurements shall be made.
The arithmetic mean of the further series of 10 measurements shall constitute the final result.
Any method may be used to measure variations of inclination, provided that its readings are accurate to within ±0.2 mrad (±0.02 per cent inclination).
The vehicle suspension and any other part likely to affect dipped-beam inclination shall be activated according to the methods described in paragraph 5.4.

The technical authorities and manufacturers may jointly propose other methods (experimental or calculation-based) for activating the vehicle suspension and other parts affecting dipped-beam inclination, especially when the test poses particular problems, provided such calculations are clearly valid.
With the vehicle standing on the measuring site, the vehicle shall be rocked continuously for at least three complete cycles.
In each rocking cycle, the rear end of the vehicle shall be pushed down first and then the front end.
Floating platforms shall be used under the wheels if their absence would lead to restriction of the suspension movement likely to affect the results of measurements.
The rocking sequence shall end with the completion of a full cycle.
Before making the measurements, the vehicle shall be allowed to come to rest spontaneously.
As an alternative to floating platforms, the same effect may be achieved by moving the vehicle backwards and forwards for at least one complete wheel revolution.
If the treatment method for category M1 vehicles described in paragraph 5.4.1. is not possible, the method described in paragraph 5.4.2.2. or 5.4.2.3. may be used.

With the vehicle standing on the measuring site and the wheels on the ground, the vehicle suspension and all other parts which may affect the dipped-beam inclination shall be activated by using a vibration rig.
The vibration rig used to activate the suspension and other parts may be a vibrating platform on which the vehicle wheels rest.

For vehicles with non-conventional suspension where the propulsion system has to be running, before making any measurement, the vehicle shall be allowed to assume its final attitude with the engine running.
The variation of the dipped-beam inclination shall be assessed for each of the different loading conditions, relative to the measured initial inclination determined in accordance with paragraph 5.2.
If the vehicle is fitted with a manual headlamp-levelling system, the system shall be adjusted to the positions specified by the manufacturer for given loading conditions (according to Annex 5).
A single measurement shall be made in each loading condition.

For all loading conditions, the variation in inclination shall be within the calculated limits (for example, within the difference between the stated initial inclination and the lower and upper limits specified for approval).
The inclination variation compliance check shall include a safety margin of 4 mrad (0.4 per cent inclination).
If the result(s) exceed(s) the limit values, a further three measurements shall be made in the loading conditions corresponding to this (these) result(s), as specified in paragraph 5.5.3.
If none of the three measured results differs by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination) from the arithmetic mean of the results, the arithmetic mean shall constitute the final result.
If any measurement differs from the arithmetic mean of the results by more than 2 mrad (0.2 per cent inclination), a further series of 10 measurements shall be made.
The arithmetic mean of the further series of 10 measurements shall constitute the final result.

For a vehicle fitted with an automatic headlamp-levelling system that has an inherent hysteresis loop, the average of the results at the top and bottom of the hysteresis loop shall be taken as the significant values.
For a vehicle fitted with an automatic headlamp-levelling system that has an inherent hysteresis loop, all measurements shall be made in accordance with paragraphs 5.5.3.1 and 5.5.3.2.

The requirements are met only if, under all loading conditions, the variation between the measured initial inclination (determined in accordance with paragraph 5.2.) and the inclination measured under each loading condition is less than the values calculated in paragraph 5.5.1. (without safety margin).

If only one of the calculated upper or lower limits of variation is exceeded, the manufacturer may choose a different value for the stated initial inclination, within the limits specified for approval.
Inclination of the dipped beam shall in all cases be produced by a simple control.
The operation of the dipped beam inclination control shall be clearly described in the owner’s handbook.

The control for adjusting the headlamp beam inclination (levelling control) shall carry symbol(s) indicating clearly the movements corresponding to the downward and upward inclination of the dipped beam.
The "0" position, which according to paragraph 6.2.6.2.2 of this Regulation has to be a "stop position", need not necessarily be at the end of the scale.

The position of lamps, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6. of UN R48, in width, in height and in length shall be checked in accordance with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of UN R48.
The values measured for the distances of the lamp positions (in width, height and length) shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
The angles of geometric visibility shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7 of this Regulation.
The values measured for the angles shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

The limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3 for the mounting of the light-signalling devices, notwithstanding that the measured values must otherwise fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10 of UN R48.
The initial downward inclination of the cut-off of the dipped beam and of the front fog lamps shall be set to the plated figure as required and shown in Annex 7.

The manufacturer shall set the initial aim to a figure different from the plated figure only where it can be shown to be representative of the type approved when tested in accordance with the procedures in Annex 6 and in particular paragraph 4.1.

The variation of the dipped-beam downward inclination as a function of the loading conditions specified in this section shall remain within the range given in the table of upper and lower inclination limits by mounting height h [m].
For a mounting height 0.5 ≤ h ≤ 0.9 m, the dipped-beam downward inclination variation with loading shall have an upper limit of -0.50 per cent and a lower limit of -(h + 1.2) per cent.

For a mounting height 0.9 < h ≤ 1.2 m, the dipped-beam downward inclination variation with loading shall have an upper limit of -(h x 2.17 - 1.45) per cent and a lower limit of -(h x 2.17 + 0.15) per cent.

For a front fog lamp with light source(s) having a total objective luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens and mounting height h < 0.8 m, the downward inclination variation with loading shall have a minimum vertical inclination of 0.7 per cent and a maximum vertical inclination of 3.3 per cent.

For a front fog lamp with light source(s) having a total objective luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens and mounting height h > 0.8 m, the downward inclination variation with loading shall have a minimum vertical inclination of 1.2 per cent and a maximum vertical inclination of 3.8 per cent.
The states of loading used for the inclination variation test shall be those indicated in Annex 5 of this Regulation, applied to every system adjusted accordingly.
The electrical connections shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle.
The lamps and tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
The aggregate maximum intensity of the main beam headlamps shall be checked by the procedure described in paragraph 6.1.9.2. of UN R48.
The value obtained from the aggregate maximum intensity check of the main beam headlamps shall be such that the requirement in paragraph 6.1.9.1. of UN R48 is fulfilled.
The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.
The lamps shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16., as well as the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, are fulfilled.

The test drive shall be carried out in clear atmosphere, i.e. good visibility with meteorological optical range MOR > 2,000 m as defined per WMO Guide to Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation.
The test drive shall be carried out with clean head-lamps.
The test course shall comprise test sections with traffic conditions, each at a speed corresponding to the relevant type of road as described in Table 1.
The test section for multi-lane roads, e.g. motorways, shall be driven at a speed of 100 ± 20 km/h.
The average length of the test sections for urban areas, multi-lane roads and country roads shall be 10 per cent, 20 per cent and 70 per cent respectively of the full test course length.
Test section A shall include a single oncoming vehicle or a single preceding vehicle, in a frequency so that the main beam will switch ON and OFF.
Test section B shall include combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations, in a frequency so that the main beam will switch ON and OFF.
Test section C shall include active and passive overtaking manoeuvres, in a frequency so that the main beam will switch ON and OFF.
Test section D shall include an oncoming bicycle as described in paragraph 6.1.9.3.1.2.
Test section E shall include combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations.
Country roads shall comprise sections having two lanes and sections having four or more lanes.
Country roads shall include junctions, hills and/or slopes, dips and winding roads.
Multi-lane roads (e.g. motorways) and country roads shall comprise sections having straight level parts with a length of more than 600 m.
Multi-lane roads (e.g. motorways) and country roads shall additionally comprise sections having curves to the left and to the right.
Dense traffic situations shall be taken into account (as specified in Annex 12 of UN R48).

The test drive shall be carried out in clear atmosphere, meaning good visibility with meteorological optical range (MOR) greater than 2,000 m, defined according to WMO Guide to Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation (Sixth Edition, pp 1.9.1/1.9.11, Geneva 1996).
The test drive shall be carried out with clean head-lamps.
The test course shall comprise test sections with traffic conditions, at speed corresponding to the relevant road type, as described in Table 2.
For multi-lane roads (e.g. motorway), the test section speed shall be 100 ± 20 km/h.
The average share of the full test course length shall be 10 per cent for urban areas, 20 per cent for multi-lane roads (e.g. motorway) and 70 per cent for country roads.
Test section A shall include a single oncoming vehicle or a single preceding vehicle, at a frequency such that the adaptive main beam will react to demonstrate the adaptation process.
Test section B shall include combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations, at a frequency such that the adaptive main beam will react to demonstrate the adaptation process.
Test section C shall include active and passive overtaking manoeuvres, at a frequency such that the adaptive main beam will react to demonstrate the adaptation process.
Test section D shall include an oncoming bicycle as described in paragraph 6.22.9.3.1.2.
Test section E shall include combined oncoming and preceding traffic situations.
Country roads shall comprise sections having two lanes and sections having four or more lanes.
Country roads shall include junctions, hills and/or slopes, dips and winding roads.
Multi-lane roads (e.g. motorways) and country roads used for the test route shall comprise sections having straight level parts with a length of more than 600 m.
Multi-lane roads and country roads used for the test route shall additionally comprise sections having curves to the left and to the right.
Dense traffic situations shall be taken into account.

For test sections A and B in the table above, the engineers conducting the tests shall evaluate and record the acceptability of the performance of the adaptation process in relation to oncoming and preceding road users.
For test sections A and B, the test engineers shall be seated in the vehicle being tested and additionally be seated in the oncoming and preceding vehicles.
For test sections A, B, C and E in the table above, the engineers conducting the tests shall evaluate Driver Assistance Projection if it is installed.

Compliance with the automatic switching conditions for dipped-beam headlamps shall be demonstrated by the applicant, by simulation or other means of verification accepted by the Type Approval Authority.
When the ambient light outside the vehicle is less than 1,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall switch ON.
When the ambient light outside the vehicle is less than 1,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall switch ON within no more than 2 seconds.

When the ambient light outside the vehicle is between 1,000 lux and 7,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps may be switched ON or OFF at the manufacturer’s discretion, with the response time at the manufacturer’s discretion.
When the ambient light outside the vehicle is more than 7,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall switch OFF.
When the ambient light outside the vehicle is more than 7,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall switch OFF within more than 5 seconds and no more than 300 seconds.

The illuminance of the ambient light outside the vehicle shall be measured on a horizontal surface, with a cosine corrected sensor located at the same height as the mounting position of the sensor on the vehicle.
The manufacturer may demonstrate the illuminance measurement method by sufficient documentation or by other means accepted by the Type Approval Authority.
The risk of collision warning shall be triggered when the relative speed is larger than 30 km/h and the Risk of Collision Time is less than 1.4 s.
The risk of collision warning may flash at 4.0 Hz +/- 1.0 Hz.
The wrong way warning shall be activated when the vehicle is entering a one-way road or a highway in opposite direction.
The wrong way warning may flash at 4.0 Hz +/- 1.0 Hz.
The lane keeping assist warning shall be activated if the vehicle unintentionally exits its lane.
The shape of the Driver Assistance Projection for the predicted trajectory may change when adapted in conformity with the requirements in paragraph 5.35.12.
An ESA may be approved, at the request of a manufacturer or his authorized representative, either as a "component" or as a "separate technical unit (STU)".
Variations in the vehicle body, meaning the presence of panels of different material where the primary material of the body is unchanged, shall be notified.
The application for approval of a vehicle type, with regard to its electromagnetic compatibility, shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer.

The vehicle manufacturer shall draw up a schedule describing all relevant vehicle electrical/electronic systems or ESAs, body styles, variations in body material, general wiring arrangements, engine variations, left-hand/right-hand drive versions and wheelbase versions.
A vehicle representative of the type to be approved shall be selected from the schedule by mutual agreement between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority.
The choice of the representative vehicle shall be based on the electrical/electronic systems offered by the manufacturer.

One or more additional vehicles may be selected from the schedule only if, by mutual agreement between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority, different electrical/electronic systems are included that are likely to have a significant effect on the vehicle's electromagnetic compatibility compared with the first representative vehicle.
The choice of vehicle(s) in conformity with paragraph 3.1.4 shall be limited to vehicle/electrical/electronic system combinations intended for actual production.
The manufacturer may supplement the type approval application with a report on the tests that have been carried out.
The Type Approval Authority may use any test data provided by the manufacturer to draw up the communication form for type approval.
If the Technical Service responsible for the type approval test carries out the test itself, a vehicle representative of the type to be approved according to paragraph 3.1.4 above shall be provided.

For vehicles of categories L6, L7, M, N, O, T, R and S, the vehicle manufacturer shall provide a statement of frequency bands, power levels, antenna positions and installation provisions for the installation of RF transmitters, even if the vehicle is not equipped with an RF transmitter at the time of type approval.
The statement of frequency bands, power levels, antenna positions and installation provisions for RF transmitters shall be noted in the information document (e.g. under item 63, Annex 2A).
The statement should cover all mobile radio services normally used in vehicles.
The information on RF transmitter frequency bands, power levels, antenna positions and installation provisions shall be made publicly available following the type approval.
Vehicle manufacturers shall provide evidence that vehicle performance is not adversely affected by RF transmitter installations.
The application for approval of an ESA type with regard to its electromagnetic compatibility shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by the manufacturer of the ESA.
The manufacturer may supplement the application for approval with a report on tests that have been carried out.
The Type Approval Authority may use the test data provided by the manufacturer with the application supplement for the purpose of drawing up the communication form for type approval.

Where the Technical Service responsible for the type approval test carries out the test itself, a sample of the ESA system representative of the type to be approved shall be provided, if necessary after discussion with the manufacturer on possible variations in the layout, number of components and number of sensors.
If the Technical Service deems it necessary, it may select a further sample.
The sample(s) submitted for ESA type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
Where applicable, any restrictions on use of the ESA should be identified.
Any restrictions on use that have been identified should be included in Annexes 2B and/or 3B.
Components sold as aftermarket equipment and intended for installation in motor vehicles need no type approval only if they are not related to immunity related functions (see paragraph 2.12.).

Where aftermarket components are exempt from type approval, the manufacturer shall issue a declaration that the ESA fulfils the requirements of this Regulation and in particular the limits defined in paragraphs 6.5., 6.6., 6.7., 6.8. and 6.9. of this Regulation.
Where the ESA is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall specify the approval number granted to this ESA according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
Where the ESA is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall specify the approval number granted to this ESA according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.

Where the ESA is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall provide a test report by a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority, stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
The alternative procedures for vehicle type approval listed under paragraph 4.1.1 may be used at the discretion of the vehicle manufacturer.
A vehicle installation may be type approved directly by following the provisions laid down in paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7 of this Regulation.
If the direct type approval procedure of paragraph 4.1.1.1 is chosen by a vehicle manufacturer, no separate testing of electrical/electronic systems or ESAs is required.
A vehicle manufacturer may obtain approval of the vehicle type by testing of individual ESAs, by demonstrating to the Type Approval Authority the matters required in this paragraph.

The vehicle manufacturer shall demonstrate to the Type Approval Authority that all relevant electrical/electronic systems or ESAs (see paragraph 3.1.3.) have been approved in accordance with this Regulation.
All relevant electrical/electronic systems or ESAs shall be installed in accordance with any conditions attached to their approvals.
A manufacturer may obtain approval according to this Regulation only if the vehicle has no equipment of the type that is subject to immunity or emission tests.
Approvals obtained under paragraph 4.1.1.3 shall not require testing.
Type approval may be granted to an ESA intended to be fitted to any vehicle type (component approval).
Type approval may be granted to an ESA intended to be fitted to a specific vehicle type or types requested by the ESA manufacturer (separate technical unit approval).
ESAs that are intentional RF transmitters and that have not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines.
If the representative vehicle fulfils the requirements of paragraph 6. and, if applicable, paragraph 7. of UN R10, type approval shall be granted.

When drawing up the communication forms referred to in paragraphs 4.2.1.2. or 4.2.2.2., the Type Approval Authority of the Contracting Party granting the approval may use a report prepared or approved by a recognized laboratory or prepared in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.
Where an ESA is (part of) a light source and the documentation specified in paragraph 3.2.10 is missing, approval of that ESA according to Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.

The approval, or refusal of approval, of a type of vehicle or ESA under this Regulation shall be notified to the Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation on a form conforming to the model in Annex 3A or 3B to this Regulation.

The approval notification shall be accompanied by photographs and/or diagrams or drawings on an appropriate scale supplied by the applicant, in a format not larger than A4 (210 x 297 mm) or folded to those dimensions.
An approval number shall be assigned to each vehicle or ESA type approved in accordance with Schedule 4 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
Electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles that are approved as units shall not be required to carry a marking under UN R10 paragraph 5.2.2.

An international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under this Regulation.
The international approval mark shall comprise the elements listed in the sub-items that follow paragraph 5.3.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
A vehicle shall be tested for radiated emissions and for immunity to radiated disturbances.
Tests for conducted emissions and for immunity to conducted disturbances shall not be required for vehicle type approval.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated emissions and for conducted emissions.
ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and for immunity to conducted disturbances.
Before testing, the Technical Service shall prepare a test plan in conjunction with the manufacturer.
The test plan shall contain at least the mode of operation, stimulated function(s), monitored function(s), pass/fail criterion(criteria) and intended emissions.

Depending on the intended operating conditions of the propulsion system, the test plan shall define the minimum number of steady state operating conditions of the vehicle, selectable by the driver or by the control system.
The test conditions shall consider multiple propulsion system operating strategies which can be activated permanently by the driver or the vehicle control system.
The test conditions shall be based on documentation provided in Annexes 2A and 2B (e.g. risk analysis).
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 4.
The vehicle manufacturer shall define the method of measurement in accordance with the Technical Service.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 32 dB microvolts/m.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall rise logarithmically from 32 dB microvolts/m to 43 dB microvolts/m with increasing frequency above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 2 to this Regulation.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m.
When broadband electromagnetic radiation measurements are made using the Annex 4 method, the vehicle-to-antenna spacing shall be 3.0 ± 0.05 m.
When measured per Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit shall be 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

When measured per Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 dBµV/m at 75 MHz, increasing logarithmically with frequency to 53 dBµV/m at 400 MHz as shown in Appendix 3 to this Regulation.
When measured per Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dBµV/m.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 5.

The items referred to as 'these' (the measurement conditions or parameters for the method in Annex 5, as the paragraph's context indicates) shall be defined by the vehicle manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.

When narrowband radiated emission measurements are made using the Annex 5 method with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band shall be 28 dB microvolts/m.

When narrowband radiated emission measurements are made using the Annex 5 method with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall be 35 dB microvolts/m.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the narrowband limit in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band shall be 38 dB microvolts/m.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the narrowband limit in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall be 45 dB microvolts/m.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the narrowband electromagnetic radiation measured values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limit.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.
When tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the radiated field strength shall be 30 V/m over at least 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the radiated field strength shall be at least 25 V/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the radiated field strength shall be 10 V/m over at least 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the radiated field strength shall be at least 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the injected current shall be 60 mA over at least 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the injected current shall be at least 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6, the vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity-related functions, as identified in paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband ESA limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband ESA limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband ESA limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband electromagnetic interference values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the ESA broadband type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic interference limit in the 30 to 75 MHz band shall be 52 dB microvolts/m at 30 MHz, decreasing logarithmically to 42 dB microvolts/m at 75 MHz.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic interference limit in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 42 dB microvolts/m at 75 MHz, increasing logarithmically to 53 dB microvolts/m at 400 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic interference limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband electromagnetic interference value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The emission of an ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2, as described in Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 1.
For positive polarity, the maximum allowed pulse amplitude of the ESA emission shall be +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
For negative polarity, the maximum allowed pulse amplitude of the ESA emission shall be -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of an ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) described in Annex 9.
The test severity for the immunity of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation, over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, shall be as given in Table 2a.
The minimum test level for the immunity of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, shall be as given in Table 2b.

During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of its "immunity related functions" in order to be considered as complying with immunity requirements.

The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10.
The immunity test of ESA representative of this type shall be performed with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile immunity test of ESA shall be evaluated according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the immunity tests for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
The starting profile test is only applicable to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, that vehicle, system or ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
Vehicles which do not have electrical/electronic systems with "immunity related functions" need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
Vehicles which do not have electrical/electronic systems with "immunity related functions" shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.4 and with Annex 6 to this Regulation.
ESAs with no immunity related functions are not required to be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
ESAs with no immunity related functions shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8 and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.
ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches, or do not include an inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines.
ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches, or do not include an inductive load shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7 without transient conducted emission testing.
RF transmitters shall be tested in the transmit mode.
Spurious emissions of RF transmitters are subject to the requirements of this Regulation.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to enable the vehicle, in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", to comply with the requirements of UN R10.

A vehicle in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be tested for radiated emissions, immunity to radiated disturbances, conducted emissions and immunity to conducted disturbances.
ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions.
ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be tested for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

Before testing, the Technical Service shall prepare, in conjunction with the manufacturer, a test plan for the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" that contains at least the mode of operation, stimulated function(s), monitored function(s), pass/fail criterion (criteria) and intended emissions.
Depending on the available charging modes of the REESS, the test plan shall define the minimum number of test conditions of the vehicle that are selectable by the driver or by the control system.
The test plan shall be based on the documentation provided in Annexes 2A and 2B (e.g. risk analysis).

A vehicle in the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" should be tested with the charging harness delivered by the manufacturer, in line with the flowcharts provided in Annexes 4, 6, 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16.
AC power mains shall be applied to the vehicle / ESA through 50 µH/50 Ω AMN(s) as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 4.
DC power mains shall be applied to the vehicle / ESA through 5 µH/50 Ω DC-charging-AN(s) as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 3.
The high voltage power line shall be applied to the ESA through a 5 µH/50 Ω HV-AN(s) as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 2.
Signal port lines, control port lines or wired network port lines should be applied to the vehicle / ESA through an AAN as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 4.
The vehicle manufacturer shall define the method of measurement in accordance with the Technical Service.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 32 dB microvolts/m.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 42 dB microvolts/m.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 dB microvolts/m at 75 MHz, increasing logarithmically with frequency to 53 dB microvolts/m, as shown in Appendix 3.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband electromagnetic radiation limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband electromagnetic radiation values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The harmonics emission on AC power lines generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 11.
The vehicle manufacturer shall define the method of measurement for harmonics emission on AC power lines in accordance with the Technical Service.

When emission measurements are made using the method described in Annex 11, the harmonic current limits for input current ≤ 16 A per phase shall be those defined in IEC 61000-3-2 and given in Table 4.
The maximum allowed harmonic currents in Table 4 shall apply to vehicles whose input current is ≤ 16 A per phase.

When harmonic measurements are made using the method described in Annex 11, the limits for equipment with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase shall be those defined in IEC 61000-3-12, as given in Table 5, Table 6 and Table 7.
Relative values of even harmonics of order lower than or equal to 12 shall be lower than 16/n %, where n is the harmonic order.
Even harmonics greater than 12 shall be taken into account in the THD and PWHD in the same way as odd harmonics.
Linear interpolation between successive values of the Short Circuit Ratio of an Equipment (Rsce) may be used.
The emission of voltage changes, voltage fluctuations and flicker on AC power lines generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 12.
The method of measurement for emission of voltage changes, voltage fluctuations and flicker on AC power lines shall be defined by the vehicle manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase not subjected to conditional connection, the value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0, as defined in IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase not subjected to conditional connection, the value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65, as defined in IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase not subjected to conditional connection, the value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms, as defined in IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase not subjected to conditional connection, the relative steady-state voltage change dc shall not exceed 3.3 per cent, as defined in IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase not subjected to conditional connection, the maximum relative voltage change dmax shall not exceed 6 per cent, as defined in IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, the limits for equipment with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase that is subjected to conditional connection are those defined in IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for equipment with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection, the value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for equipment with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection, the value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for equipment with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection, the value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for equipment with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection, the relative steady-state voltage change dc shall not exceed 3.3 per cent.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 12, for equipment with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection, the maximum relative voltage change dmax shall not exceed 6 per cent.
The emission of radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC or DC power lines generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 13.
The method of measurement for radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC or DC power lines shall be defined by the vehicle manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 13, the limits on AC power lines shall be those defined in IEC 61000-6-3 and given in Table 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 13, the maximum allowed radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC power lines shall not exceed the Table 8 values: quasi-peak limit of 66 to 56 dBµV over 0.15 to 0.5 MHz (linearly decreasing with logarithm of frequency), 56 dBµV over 0.5 to 5 MHz, and 60 dBµV over 5 to 30 MHz; average limit of 56 to 46 dBµV over 0.15 to 0.5 MHz (linearly decreasing with logarithm of frequency), 46 dBµV over 0.5 to 5 MHz, and 50 dBµV over 5 to 30 MHz.
Where measurements of radiofrequency conducted disturbances are made using the method described in Annex 13, the limits on DC power lines shall be those defined in IEC 61000-6-3 and given in Table 9.

For specific vehicles which are charged only with charging stations located in an area characterized by a separate power network, supplied from a high or medium voltage transformer dedicated for the supply of the installation (e.g. buses, heavy duty trucks), the limits from IEC 61000-6-4 shall be applied for emission of radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC or DC power ports.

The manufacturer shall provide a statement that the vehicle can be used in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" only in an area characterized by a separate power network, supplied from a high or medium voltage transformer, dedicated for the supply of the installation.
The manufacturer shall provide a statement that the vehicle shall be charged in a non-residential environment only.
The information on the vehicle charging conditions stated by the manufacturer shall be made publicly available following the type approval.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 13, the limits on AC power lines shall be those defined in IEC 61000-6-4 and given in Table 10.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 13, the limits for radiofrequency conducted disturbances on DC power lines shall be those defined in IEC 61000-6-4 and given in Table 11.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the field strength shall be at least 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the field strength shall be 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the field strength shall be at least 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 with the ISO 11451-4 BCI method, the current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 with the ISO 11451-4 BCI method, the current shall be at least 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", as defined in paragraph 2.2. of Annex 6, for the vehicle type to be considered as complying with immunity requirements.
The immunity of the vehicle representative of its type to Electrical Fast Transient/Burst disturbances conducted along its AC and DC power lines shall be tested by the method described in Annex 15.

If the EFT/burst immunity tests are made using the methods described in Annex 15, the immunity test level for AC or DC power lines shall be ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit, with a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, a hold time (Th) of 50 ns, and a repetition rate of 5 kHz, applied for at least 1 minute.

During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 15, the vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of the "immunity related functions", as defined in paragraph 2.1.2. of Annex 15.
The immunity to surge conducted along AC/DC power lines of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 16.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 16, the surge immunity test voltage for AC power lines shall be ±2 kV in open circuit between line and earth and ±1 kV between lines.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 16, each AC power line surge shall have a rise time (Tr) of 1.2 µs and a hold time (Th) of 50 µs.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 16, each AC power line surge shall be applied five times with a maximum delay of 1 minute between each pulse.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 16, the AC power line surge shall be applied at the phases 0, 90, 180 and 270°.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 16, the surge immunity test voltage for DC power lines shall be ±0.5 kV in open circuit between line and earth and ±0.5 kV between lines.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 16, each DC power line surge shall have a rise time (Tr) of 1.2 µs and a hold time (Th) of 50 µs.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 16, each DC power line surge shall be applied five times with a maximum delay of 1 minute.

A vehicle representative of its type shall be considered as complying with the immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 16, there is no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1.2. of Annex 16.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic interference limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic interference limit in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 52 to 63 dBµV/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic interference limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 63 dBµV/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband electromagnetic interference values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The harmonics emission on AC power lines generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 17.
The method of measurement for the harmonics emission on AC power lines shall be defined by the manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 17, the limits for input current ≤ 16 A per phase shall be those defined in IEC 61000-3-2 and given in Table 12.

For odd harmonics, the maximum authorized harmonic current (input current ≤ 16 A per phase) shall not exceed 2.3 A for n = 3, 1.14 A for n = 5, 0.77 A for n = 7, 0.40 A for n = 9, 0.33 A for n = 11, 0.21 A for n = 13, and 0.15x15/n A for 15 ≤ n ≤ 39.
For even harmonics, the maximum authorized harmonic current (input current ≤ 16 A per phase) shall not exceed 1.08 A for n = 2, 0.43 A for n = 4, 0.30 A for n = 6, and 0.23x8/n A for 8 ≤ n ≤ 40.

If harmonic emission measurements are made using the method described in Annex 17, the harmonic current limits for input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase shall be those defined in IEC 61000-3-12 and given in Tables 13, 14 and 15.

For single-phase or other than balanced three-phase equipment with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase, the maximum allowed individual harmonic current (I3 to I13), THD and PWHD values, as a function of minimum Rsce, shall be those given in Table 13.

For balanced three-phase equipment with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase, the maximum allowed individual harmonic current (I5 to I13), THD and PWHD values, as a function of minimum Rsce, shall be those given in Table 14.

For balanced three-phase equipment under specific conditions with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase, the maximum allowed individual harmonic current (I5 to I13), THD and PWHD values, as a function of minimum Rsce, shall be those given in Table 15.
For the equipment covered by Tables 13, 14 and 15, the relative value of each even harmonic of order n lower than or equal to 12 shall be lower than 16/n %.
Even harmonics greater than 12 shall be taken into account in the THD and PWHD in the same way as odd harmonics.
Linear interpolation between successive values of Rsce may be used to determine the harmonic limits in Tables 13, 14 and 15.
The emission of voltage changes, voltage fluctuations and flicker on AC power lines generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 18.
The method of measurement for the emission of voltage changes, voltage fluctuations and flicker on AC power lines shall be defined by the ESA manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.

When measurements are made using the method in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and equipment not subjected to conditional connection, the short-term flicker value Pst shall not be greater than 1.0 (limit per IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5).
