When measurements are made using the method in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and equipment not subjected to conditional connection, the long-term flicker value Plt shall not be greater than 0.65 (limit per IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5).

When measurements are made using the method in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and equipment not subjected to conditional connection, the value of d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms (limit per IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5).

When measurements are made using the method in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and equipment not subjected to conditional connection, the relative steady-state voltage change dc shall not exceed 3.3 per cent (limit per IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5).

When measurements are made using the method in Annex 18, for rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and equipment not subjected to conditional connection, the maximum relative voltage change dmax shall not exceed 6 per cent (limit per IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5).

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, the emission limits for ESA with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase that are subjected to conditional connection shall be those defined in IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, the Pst value of an ESA with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection shall not be greater than 1.0.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, the Plt value of an ESA with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection shall not be greater than 0.65.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, the d(t) value of an ESA with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection shall not exceed 3.3 per cent during a voltage change for more than 500 ms.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, the relative steady-state voltage change dc of an ESA with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection shall not exceed 3.3 per cent.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 18, the maximum relative voltage change dmax of an ESA with rated current >16 A and ≤75 A per phase subjected to conditional connection shall not exceed 6 per cent.
The emission of radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC or DC power lines generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 19.
The method of measurement for radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC or DC power lines shall be defined by the ESA manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.

When radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC power lines are measured using the method described in Annex 19, the limits on AC power lines shall be those defined in IEC 61000-6-3 and given in Table 16.
When radiofrequency conducted disturbance measurements are made using the method described in Annex 19, the limits on DC power lines shall be those defined in IEC 61000-6-3 and given in Table 17.
For DC power lines measured per Annex 19, the radiofrequency conducted disturbance in the 0.15 to 0.5 MHz band shall not exceed 79 dBµV quasi-peak and 66 dBµV average.
For DC power lines measured per Annex 19, the radiofrequency conducted disturbance in the 0.5 to 30 MHz band shall not exceed 73 dBµV quasi-peak and 60 dBµV average.
The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to Electrical Fast Transient/Burst disturbances conducted along AC and DC power lines shall be tested by the method described in Annex 21.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the immunity test level for AC or DC power lines shall be ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit.

If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the electrical fast transient/burst pulses applied to AC or DC power lines shall have a rise time (Tr) of 5 ns, a hold time (Th) of 50 ns and a repetition rate of 5 kHz.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 21, the electrical fast transient/burst immunity test on AC or DC power lines shall be applied for at least 1 minute.

During the electrical fast transient/burst immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 21, the ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of the charging function as defined in paragraph 2.1. of Annex 21 in order to be considered as complying with the immunity requirements.
The immunity to surge conducted along AC / DC power lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 22.
If tests are made using the methods described in Annex 22, the AC power line surge immunity test voltage shall be ±2 kV open circuit between line and earth and ±1 kV between lines.
For AC power lines, the surge immunity test voltage shall be ±2 kV in open circuit between line and earth and ±1 kV between lines, when tests are made using the Annex 22 methods.
For AC power lines, the surge shall have a rise time (Tr) of 1.2 µs and a hold time (Th) of 50 µs when tests are made using the Annex 22 methods.
For AC power lines, each surge shall be applied five times with a maximum delay of 1 minute between each pulse when tests are made using the Annex 22 methods.
For AC power lines, the surge shall be applied at the phases 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° when tests are made using the Annex 22 methods.
For DC power lines, the surge immunity test voltage shall be ±0.5 kV in open circuit between line and earth and ±0.5 kV between lines, when tests are made using the Annex 22 methods.
For DC power lines, the surge shall have a rise time (Tr) of 1.2 µs and a hold time (Th) of 50 µs when tests are made using the Annex 22 methods.
For DC power lines, each surge shall be applied five times with a maximum delay of 1 minute when tests are made using the Annex 22 methods.
During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 22, the ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of the charging function as defined in paragraph 2.1 of Annex 22.
The emission of an ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2:2011, as described in Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 18.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of an ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) described in Annex 9.
The ESA immunity test levels in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be the levels given in Table 19a.
The minimum ESA immunity test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be the level given in Table 19b.

The ESA representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there is no degradation of performance of the charging function as defined in paragraph 2.3. of Annex 9.
The immunity of an ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) specified in ISO 7637-2.
The ESA immunity test shall be performed as described in Annex 10 using the test levels given in Table 20.

Vehicles and/or ESA intended for "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" in the configuration connected to a DC-charging station, with a DC network cable (between the DC charging station and the vehicle plug) shorter than 30 m, are not required to fulfil the requirements of paragraphs 7.5., 7.8., 7.9., 7.13., 7.15., and 7.16.

Where the exemption in paragraph 7.20.1 applies, the manufacturer shall provide a statement that the vehicle and/or ESA can be used in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" only with DC network cables shorter than 30 m.
The statement on use of the vehicle and/or ESA only with DC network cables shorter than 30 m shall be made publicly available following type approval.

Vehicles and/or ESA intended to be used in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" in the configuration connected to a local/private DC-charging station without additional participants shall not be required to fulfil the requirements of paragraphs 7.5., 7.8., 7.9., 7.13., 7.15., and 7.16.

For vehicles and/or ESA exempted under paragraph 7.20.2., the manufacturer shall provide a statement that the vehicle and/or ESA can be used in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" only with a local/private DC charging station without additional participants.
The statement on use only with a local/private DC charging station without additional participants shall be made publicly available following type approval.

Where a vehicle manufacturer has obtained type approval for a vehicle installation and wishes to fit an additional or substitutional electrical/electronic system or ESA that has already received approval under this Regulation, the vehicle approval may be extended without further testing, provided the system or ESA is installed in accordance with any conditions attached to its approval.
The additional or substitutional electrical/electronic system or ESA fitted under this paragraph shall be considered as part of the vehicle for conformity of production purposes.

Where the additional or substitution part(s) has (have) not received approval under this Regulation and testing is considered necessary, the whole vehicle shall be deemed to conform if the new or revised part(s) can be shown to conform to the relevant requirements of paragraph 6 and, if applicable, of paragraph 7.

Where the additional or substitution part(s) has (have) not received approval under this Regulation and testing is considered necessary, the whole vehicle shall be deemed to conform if, in a comparative test, the new part can be shown not to be likely to adversely affect the conformity of the vehicle type.

The addition by a vehicle manufacturer to an approved vehicle of standard domestic or business equipment (other than mobile communication equipment) that conforms to other Regulations, and whose installation, substitution or removal follows the recommendations of the equipment and vehicle manufacturers, shall not invalidate the vehicle approval.

Vehicle manufacturers may fit communication equipment in accordance with suitable installation guidelines developed by the vehicle manufacturer and/or the manufacturer(s) of such communication equipment.
If requested by the test authority, the vehicle manufacturer shall provide evidence that vehicle performance is not adversely affected by such transmitters.

The evidence required for communication transmitters may be a statement that the power levels and installation are such that the immunity levels of this Regulation offer sufficient protection when subject to transmission alone (excluding transmission in conjunction with the tests specified in paragraph 6).
This Regulation does not authorize the use of a communication transmitter where other requirements on such equipment or its use apply.
The conformity of production procedures shall comply with the procedures set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
Vehicles, components or ESAs approved under UN R10 shall be manufactured so as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraph 6 and, where applicable, paragraph 7.

Conformity of production of the vehicle, component or separate technical unit shall be checked on the basis of the data contained in the type approval communication form(s) set out in Annex 3A and/or Annex 3B to this Regulation.
If the Type Approval Authority is not satisfied with the checking procedure of the manufacturer, then paragraphs 9.3.1, 9.3.2 and 9.3.3 of the Conformity of production section apply.

When verifying the conformity of a vehicle taken from the series, production is deemed to conform to this Regulation for broadband and narrowband electromagnetic disturbances if the measured levels do not exceed the reference limits in paragraphs 6.2.2.1., 6.2.2.2., 6.3.2.1., 6.3.2.2. and, if applicable, 7.2.2.1. and 7.2.2.2. by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).

When verifying the conformity of a component or ESA taken from the series, production is deemed to conform to this Regulation for broadband and narrowband electromagnetic disturbances if the measured levels do not exceed the reference limits in paragraphs 6.5.2.1., 6.6.2.1. and, if applicable, the following paragraph (the reference is truncated in the source text) by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).

When verifying the conformity of a vehicle, component or ESA taken from the series, production is deemed to conform to this Regulation's electromagnetic radiation immunity requirements if the vehicle or ESA shows no degradation relating to direct control of the vehicle that could be observed by the driver or other road user.

For the conformity check in 9.3.2, the vehicle must be in the state defined in Annex 6, paragraph 4, and subjected to a field strength in V/m up to 80 per cent of the reference limits in paragraph 6.4.2.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.7.2.1 for vehicles, or in paragraph 6.8.2.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.18.2.1 for ESAs.

A component or STU taken from the series, when its conformity is being verified, is deemed to conform to the immunity-to-conducted-disturbances requirements of this Regulation only if it shows no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1.

A component or STU taken from the series, when its conformity is being verified, is deemed to conform to the emission requirements of this Regulation only if it does not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1.

The approval granted for a type of vehicle, component or separate technical unit under this Regulation may be withdrawn if the requirements laid down in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, paragraph 7. are not complied with, or if the selected vehicles fail to pass the tests provided for in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.

If a Party to the Agreement applying this Regulation withdraws an approval it has previously granted, that Party shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation of the withdrawal by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annexes 3A and 3B to this Regulation.

If the holder of an approval permanently ceases to manufacture a type of vehicle or ESA approved in accordance with this Regulation, the holder shall inform the Type Approval Authority which granted the approval.

The Type Approval Authority which granted the approval shall notify the other Parties to the 1958 Agreement which apply this Regulation, by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annexes 3A and 3B to this Regulation.
Every modification of the vehicle or ESA type shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority that granted approval of the vehicle type.

Notice of conformation of approval or of refusal of approval, accompanied by particulars of the modifications, shall be communicated by the procedure indicated in paragraph 4 of UN R10 to the Parties to the Agreement applying UN R10.
The Type Approval Authority granting an approval extension shall assign a serial number to that extension.

The Type Approval Authority granting an approval extension shall notify the other Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation of the serial-numbered extension by means of a communication form conforming to the models in Annexes 3A and 3B to this Regulation.
Contracting Parties applying UN Regulation No. 10 shall not refuse to grant UN type-approvals according to any preceding series of amendments to this UN Regulation or extensions thereof.

The Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation shall communicate to the United Nations Secretariat the names and addresses of the Technical Services conducting approval tests and of the Type Approval Authorities which grant approvals and to which forms certifying approval or extension, refusal or withdrawal of approval, issued in other countries, are to be sent.
The vehicle broadband and narrowband reference limits in Appendices 2 to 7 shall be measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.

For vehicle broadband emissions at 10 m antenna-vehicle separation (Appendix 2, referenced by paragraphs 6.2.2.1. and 7.2.2.1.), the limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth is E = 32 over 30-75 MHz, E = 32 + 15.13 log (F/75) over 75-400 MHz, and E = 43 over 400-1,000 MHz.

For vehicle broadband emissions at 3 m antenna-vehicle separation (Appendix 3, referenced by paragraphs 6.2.2.2. and 7.2.2.2.), the limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth is E = 42 over 30-75 MHz, E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) over 75-400 MHz, and E = 53 over 400-1,000 MHz.

For vehicle narrowband emissions at 10 m antenna-vehicle separation (Appendix 4, referenced by paragraph 6.3.2.1.), the limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth is E = 28 over 30-230 MHz and E = 35 over 230-1,000 MHz.

For vehicle narrowband emissions at 3 m antenna-vehicle separation (Appendix 5, referenced by paragraph 6.3.2.2.), the limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth is E = 38 over 30-230 MHz and E = 45 over 230-1,000 MHz.

For electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) broadband emissions (Appendix 6, referenced by paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), the limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth is E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) over 30-75 MHz, E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) over 75-400 MHz, and E = 63 over 400-1,000 MHz.

For electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) narrowband emissions (Appendix 7, referenced by paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth is E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) over 30-75 MHz, E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) over 75-400 MHz, and E = 53 over 400-1,000 MHz.
For an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω artificial network (AN) as defined in Figure 1 shall be used.
The artificial network(s) (AN) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The grounding connection of the artificial network(s) (AN) shall be bonded to the ground plane.
The measurement ports of the artificial network(s) (AN) shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
The artificial network impedance ZPB, with a tolerance of ±20 %, shall conform to the characteristic shown in Figure 2 over the measurement frequency range of 0.1 MHz to 100 MHz.
The artificial network impedance ZPB shall be measured between terminals P and B (per Figure 1) with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port, with terminals A and B short circuited.
For an ESA powered by HV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω HV-AN as defined in Figure 3 shall be used.
The HV-AN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The grounding connection of the HV-AN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane.
Measurement ports of HV-AN(s) shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
The HV-AN impedance ZPB shall be within ±20 % of the impedance shown in Figure 2 over the measurement frequency range of 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz.
The HV-AN impedance ZPB shall be measured between the “ESA HV” and “GND” terminals (of Figure 3) with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port and with the “HV supply” and “GND” terminals short circuited.
If unshielded HV-ANs are used in a single shielded box, an inner shield shall be provided between the HV-ANs as described in Figure 4.
An optional impedance matching network may be used to simulate the common mode / differential mode impedance seen by the ESA plugged on the HV power supply, as shown in Figure 5.
For a vehicle/ESA in charging mode connected to a DC power supply, a 5 µH / 50 Ω DC-charging-AN as defined in Figure 6 shall be used.
The measurement ports of the DC-charging-AN(s) shall be terminated with 50 Ω loads.
The DC-charging-AN impedance ZPB shall follow the characteristic shown in Figure 7, with a tolerance of ±20 % in the measurement frequency range of 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz.

The DC-charging-AN impedance ZPB shall be measured between the terminals “Vehicle/ESA HV” and “GND” (of Figure 6) with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port and with terminals “HV Supply” and “GND” short circuited.
The value of C2 shall be 1 µF by default; if another value of C2 is used, it shall be justified.
Resistor R2 (1 MΩ) shall discharge C2 to > 50 Vdc within 60 s.
For a vehicle or ESA in charging mode connected to an AC power mains, a 50 µH / 50 Ω AMN as defined in CISPR 16-1-2 Clause 4.4 shall be used.
The measurement ports of the AMN(s) shall be terminated with 50 Ω loads.
The measurement ports of the asymmetric artificial network(s) shall be terminated with 50 Ω loads.
The asymmetric artificial networks defined in paragraphs 5.1., 5.2., 5.3. and 5.4. of this appendix shall be used for unshielded signal/control port lines and/or wired network port lines.
If shielded signal/control port lines are used, shielded asymmetric artificial networks defined in CISPR 32:2015 Annex G, Figures G.10 and G.11 should be used.

The asymmetric artificial network (AAN) shall be connected between the vehicle and the charging station, or any auxiliary equipment (AE) used to simulate communication, and its design is defined in CISPR 16-1-2 Annex E Clause E.2 (T network circuit).
The AAN shall have a common mode impedance of 150 Ω.
The value of longitudinal conversion loss (LCL) should be predetermined by measurements or be defined by the manufacturer of the charging station/charging harness.
The selected value for LCL and its origin shall be stated in the test report.
An AAN is not required for CAN communication if an original charging station can be used for the test.
If the CAN communication is emulated and the presence of the AAN prevents proper CAN communication, no AAN should be used.
If an original charging station can be used for the test, an AAN and/or AMN/DC-charging-AN need not be provided for PLC communication.

If the presence of the AMN/DC-charging-AN prevents proper PLC communication with the original charging station, or if PLC communication must be simulated by auxiliary equipment (e.g. a PLC modem) instead of the original charging station, an AAN shall be added between the AE (e.g. the PLC modem) and the AMN/DC-charging-AN output (vehicle side), as shown in Figure 9.
For emission tests, an attenuator shall be located between the powerline and the PLC modem on the AE side of the circuit, in order to minimize emission from the vehicle's PLC modem.
The attenuator shall consist of two resistors which, in combination with the input/output impedance of the PLC modem, form the attenuation network.
The resistor values shall be selected according to the design impedance of the PLC modem and the allowed attenuation for the PLC system.
A special AAN as defined in Figure 10 shall be used for a Signal/Control port with PLC on the control pilot.
The AAN shall provide a common mode impedance of 150 Ω ± 20 Ω over 150 kHz to 30 MHz on the control pilot line, assuming a design impedance of the modem of 100 Ω.
A communication simulation is typically used in combination with the AAN network.

The attenuator formed by the resistors and the design impedance of the PLC modem shall ensure that the signal on the charging harness is dominated by the vehicle's communication signals rather than the AE PLC modem.

The inductance and capacitance values of the networks added for PLC on the control pilot (Figure 10) shall not induce any malfunction of communication between the vehicle and AE or the charging station.
The inductance and capacitance values may need to be adapted to ensure proper communication.
If PLC communication is emulated and the presence of the AAN prevents proper PLC communication, no AAN should be used.
The values of the three resistors shall be set according to the design impedance of the PLC modem connected at the AE side.
A special AAN as defined in Figure 11 shall be used for the Signal/Control port with control pilot.
The AAN shall provide a common mode impedance of 150 Ω ± 20 Ω (150 kHz to 30 MHz) on the control pilot line, between A and B/D.
The inductance and capacitance values of the control pilot networks shown in Figure 11 shall not induce any malfunction of communication between vehicle and charging station.
The inductance and capacitance values of the control pilot networks may be adapted as necessary to ensure proper communication between vehicle and charging station.
If control pilot communication is emulated and the presence of the AAN prevents proper control pilot communication, no AAN should be used.
The information document for type approval of a vehicle with respect to electromagnetic compatibility shall be supplied in triplicate.
The information document for type approval of a vehicle with respect to electromagnetic compatibility shall include a list of contents.
Any drawings in the information document shall be supplied in appropriate scale and in sufficient detail.
If the submission is paper based, the documents shall be on size A4 or in a folder of A4 format.
Electronic submissions of the information document may be of any standard size.
Any photographs in the information document shall show sufficient detail.
If the systems, components or separate technical units have electronic controls, information concerning their performance shall be supplied in the information document.

Where appropriate, the applicant for type approval shall supply a list with make(s) and type(s) of all electrical and/or electronic components concerned by UN R10 (see paragraphs 2.9. and 2.10. of this Regulation) and not previously listed.

Where appropriate, the applicant for type approval shall supply schematics or a drawing of the general arrangement of electrical and/or electronic components (concerned by UN R10) and the general wiring harness arrangement.
Where appropriate, the applicant for type approval shall supply a description of the vehicle chosen to represent the type, stating body style, left or right hand drive, and wheelbase.

Where appropriate, the applicant for type approval shall supply the relevant test report(s) provided by the manufacturer from a test laboratory accredited to ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type-Approval Authority for the purpose of drawing up the type approval certificate.
The information listed in this Annex 2B information document, where applicable, shall be supplied in triplicate.
The information document for type approval of an electric/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) with respect to electromagnetic compatibility shall include a list of contents.
Any drawings in the information document for ESA type approval with respect to electromagnetic compatibility shall be supplied in appropriate scale and in sufficient detail.
If the submission is paper based, the documents shall be on size A4 or in a folder of A4 format.
Electronic submissions of the information document may be of any standard size.
Photographs in the information document for ESA type approval, if any, shall show sufficient detail.
If the systems, components or separate technical units have electronic controls, information concerning their performance shall be supplied in the information document.

If the means of identification of type contains characters not relevant to describe the component or separate technical unit types covered by this information document, those characters shall be represented in the documentation by the symbol "?" (e.g. ABC??123??).
The ESA shall be approved as a component/STU.
The communication concerning approval, extension, refusal, withdrawal or definitive discontinuation of an ESA type under UN Regulation No. 10 shall be in a maximum format of A4 (210 x 297 mm).
The test method described in this annex shall only be applied to vehicles.
Unless otherwise stated in Annex 4, the broadband emissions test for electrical or electronic systems fitted to the vehicle shall be performed according to CISPR 12.
For two-wheeled vehicles tested in the vehicle state during tests, a non-conductive insulating support with a thickness of 5 – 20 mm shall be used between the stand and the ground plane.
The engine shall be in operation according to CISPR 12 during the test.

For a vehicle with an electric propulsion motor or hybrid propulsion system, where operation according to CISPR 12 is not appropriate (e.g. busses, trucks, two- and three-wheel vehicles), transmission shafts, belts or chains may be disconnected to achieve the same operation condition for the propulsion.

If the operating mode defined in CISPR 12 (i.e. 40 km/h) does not activate all traction motors or auxiliary battery charging engines, an alternative steady state operating mode shall be agreed between the Technical Service and the vehicle manufacturer.
All equipment capable of generating broadband emissions that can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger should be in operation at maximum load (e.g. wiper motors or fans).
The horn and electric window motors are excluded from the requirement to be in operation at maximum load, because they are not used continuously.

For the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the vehicle shall be tested in the charging mode configuration (if available on vehicle) as defined in the flowchart of Figure 1.
In the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", where the vehicle has multiple batteries, the average state of charge of the batteries shall be considered.
In the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the vehicle shall be immobilized.
In the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the engine(s) (ICE and / or electrical engine) shall be OFF and in charging mode.
In the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", all other equipment which can be switched ON by the driver or passengers shall be OFF.

The test set-up for connecting the vehicle in the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall follow Figures 3a to 3h of Appendix 1 to this Annex, depending on AC or DC charging mode, location of charging plug and charging with or without communication.
The power mains socket(s) shall be placed on the ground plane (for ALSE) or on the floor (for OTS) of the test site.
The length of the harness between the power mains socket and the AMN(s) shall be kept as short as possible, without necessarily being aligned with the charging harness.
The power mains harness shall be placed as close as possible to the ground plane (for ALSE) or the floor (for OTS).
Power mains shall be applied to the vehicle through 50 µH/50 Ω artificial networks (AMN(s)).
The AMN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane (ALSE) or on the floor (OTS).
The case of the AMN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane (ALSE) or connected to the protective earth (OTS, e.g. an earth rod).
The measuring port of each AMN shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
The power charging harness shall be placed in a straight line between the AMN(s) and the vehicle charging plug.
The power charging harness shall be routed perpendicularly to the vehicle longitudinal axis.
The projected harness length from the side of the AMN(s) to the side of the vehicle shall be 0,8 (+0,2 / -0) m.
For a longer cable, the extraneous length of the power charging harness shall be Z-folded symmetrically.
No contact or overlap shall be allowed between the windings of the Z-folded cable.
The width of the Z-folded cable shall be between 500 mm and 1 000 mm.

If Z-folding is impractical because of cable bulk or stiffness, or because testing is done at a user's installation, the disposition of the excess cable length shall be precisely noted in the test report.
The charging harness at the vehicle side shall hang vertically at a distance of 100 (+200 / -0) mm from the vehicle body.
The whole harness shall be placed on a non-conductive, low relative permittivity (dielectric-constant) material with εr ≤ 1,4.
The whole harness shall be placed at (100 ± 25) mm above the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS).
The charging station may be placed either inside the test site or outside the test site.
If the local/private communication between the vehicle and the charging station can be simulated, the charging station may be replaced by a supply from the AC power mains network.
In both cases (charging station inside or outside the test site, or replaced by AC mains supply), the power mains and communication or signal line socket(s) shall be placed in the test site.
The power mains and communication or signal line socket(s) shall be placed on the ground plane (ALSE) or on the floor (OTS).

The length of the harness between the power mains / local/private communication socket and the AMN(s) / DC-charging-AN(s) / AAN(s) shall be kept as short as possible, but need not be aligned with the charging harness.
The harness between the power mains / local/private communication socket and the AMN(s) / DC-charging-AN(s) / AAN(s) shall be placed as close as possible to the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS).
If the charging station is placed inside the test site, the harness at the charging station side shall hang vertically down to the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS).

If the charging station is placed inside the test site, the extraneous length of the harness between the charging station and the power mains / local/private communication socket shall be placed as close as possible to the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS) and Z-folded if necessary.

If placing the excess cable close to the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS) and Z-folding it is impractical because of cable bulk or stiffness, or because testing is done at a user installation, the disposition of the excess cable shall be precisely noted in the test report.
The charging station should be placed outside the 3 dB beamwidth of the receiving antenna.

If placing the charging station outside the 3 dB beamwidth of the receiving antenna is not technically feasible, the charging station may be placed behind a panel of absorbers, but not between the antenna and the vehicle.
AC power mains shall be applied to the vehicle through 50 µH/50 Ω AMN(s) as specified in Appendix 8, paragraph 4.
DC power mains shall be applied to the vehicle through 5 µH/50 Ω High Voltage Artificial Networks (DC-charging-AN(s)) as specified in Appendix 8, paragraph 3.
The AMN(s) / DC-charging-AN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane (ALSE) or on the floor (OTS).
The cases of the AMN(s) / DC-charging-AN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane (ALSE) or connected to the protective earth (OTS, e.g. an earth rod).
The measuring port of each AMN / DC-charging-AN shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
Local/private communication lines connected to signal/control ports and lines connected to wired network ports shall be applied to the vehicle through AAN(s).
For a signal/control port with symmetric lines, the AAN used shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.1.
For a wired network port with PLC on power lines, the AAN used shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.2.
For a signal/control port with PLC (technology) on control pilot, the AAN used shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.3.
For a signal/control port with control pilot, the AAN used shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.4.
The AAN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The case of the AAN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane (ALSE) or connected to the protective earth (OTS, e.g. an earth rod).
The measuring port of each AAN shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
If a charging station is used, AAN(s) are not required for the signal/control ports and/or for the wired network ports.
The local/private communication lines between the vehicle and the charging station shall be connected to the auxiliary equipment on the charging station side to work as designed.
If communication is emulated and the presence of the AAN prevents proper communication, no AAN should be used.
The power charging local/private communication harness shall be laid out in a straight line between the AMN(s) / DC-charging-AN(s) / AAN(s) and the vehicle charging socket.
The power charging local/private communication harness shall be routed perpendicularly to the vehicle's longitudinal axis.
The projected harness length from the side of the AMN(s) to the side of the vehicle shall be 0,8 (+0,2 / -0) m.
For a longer cable, the extraneous length of the power charging local/private communication harness shall be Z-folded symmetrically.
No contact or overlap shall be allowed between the windings of the Z-folded cable.
The width of the Z-folded cable shall be between 500 mm and 1 000 mm.

If it is impractical to Z-fold the extraneous cable length because of cable bulk or stiffness, or because the testing is being done at a user's installation, the disposition of the excess cable length shall be precisely noted in the test report.
The power charging local/private communication harness at vehicle side shall hang vertically at a distance of 100 (+200 / -0) mm from the vehicle body.
The whole harness shall be placed on a non-conductive, low relative permittivity (dielectric-constant) material with εr ≤ 1,4.
The whole harness shall be placed at (100 ± 25) mm above the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS).
As an alternative to the CISPR 12 requirements for vehicles of category L, the test surface may be any location that fulfils the conditions shown in Figure 2 of the Appendix to this Annex.
When the alternative test surface is used, the measuring equipment shall lie outside the part shown in Figure 1 of Appendix 1 to this Annex.
Absorber lined shielded enclosures (ALSE) and an outdoor test site (OTS) may be used for the test.
Measurements may be performed with either quasi-peak detectors or peak detectors.
The limits given in paragraphs 6.2 and 7.2 of this Regulation shall apply to measurements made with quasi-peak detectors.
If peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied to the measurements.
The measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.
The measurement parameters used shall be those defined in Table 1 (spectrum analyser parameters) and Table 2 (scanning receiver parameters).
Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments that meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1 may be used for conformity measurements.
FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
If FFT-based instruments are used, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
For purely broadband disturbances, the maximum frequency step size of a scanning receiver may be increased up to a value not greater than the bandwidth value.
The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.

If the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may divide the frequency range into 14 frequency bands (30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz) and perform tests at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band to confirm that the vehicle meets the requirements of this Annex.

For configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", if the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type-Approval Authority for all the available charging mode configurations defined in 2.2, the Technical Service may perform tests for only one of the available charging mode configurations defined in 2.2.

For configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" under the same conditions of whole-band measurement data from an ISO 17025-accredited laboratory recognized by the Type-Approval Authority for all charging mode configurations defined in 2.2, the Technical Service may divide the frequency range into 14 frequency bands (30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz) and perform tests at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band to confirm that the vehicle meets the requirements of this Annex.
If the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the vehicle and not to background radiation.

For each of the 14 frequency bands, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal and vertical polarization and antenna location on the left and right-hand sides of the vehicle) shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
Measurements shall be made on both the left and right sides of the vehicle.
Multiple antenna positions may be required for both 10 m and 3 m antenna distances, depending on the vehicle length.
The same antenna positions shall be used for both horizontal and vertical polarization measurements.
The number of antenna positions and the position of the antenna with respect to the vehicle shall be documented in the test report.
If the vehicle length is smaller than the 3 dB beamwidth of the antenna, the antenna shall be aligned with the middle of the total vehicle.
If the vehicle length is greater than the 3 dB beamwidth of the antenna, multiple antenna positions shall be used to cover the total length of the vehicle.
The number of antenna positions N shall be chosen so that condition (1) is met.
When N is greater than 1, the antenna positions shall be symmetric with respect to the vehicle perpendicular axis.
The test method described in Annex 5 shall be applied only to vehicles.
The test method described in Annex 5 shall not be applied to the vehicle configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid".
Unless otherwise stated in Annex 5, the narrowband electromagnetic emissions test shall be performed according to CISPR 12.
The ignition switch of the vehicle shall be switched on.
The engine shall not be operating.
For two-wheeled vehicles, a non-conductive insulating support with a thickness of 5–20 mm shall be used between the stand and the ground plane.
With the vehicle stationary, all of the vehicle's electronic systems shall be in normal operating mode.
All equipment that can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger, with internal oscillators > 9 kHz or repetitive signals, should be in normal operation.
Absorber lined shielded enclosures (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS) may be used as the test facility.
Measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
Measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.
The measurement parameters to be used shall be as defined in Table 1 and Table 2.
Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments that meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1 may be used for conformity measurements.
FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
When using FFT-based instruments, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
When a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.

If the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may divide the frequency range into 14 frequency bands (30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz) and perform tests at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band to confirm that the vehicle meets the requirements of this Annex.

In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that the exceedance is due to the vehicle and not to background radiation, including broadband radiation from any ESA.

For each of the 14 frequency bands, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal and vertical polarization and antenna location on the left and right-hand sides of the vehicle) shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
Measurements shall be made on both the left and right sides of the vehicle.
Multiple antenna positions may be required, for both 10 m and 3 m antenna distance, depending on the vehicle length.
The same antenna positions shall be used for both horizontal and vertical polarization measurements.
The position of the antenna with respect to the vehicle shall be documented in the test report.
The number of antenna positions N shall be chosen so that condition (1) is met.
If the vehicle length is smaller than the 3 dB beamwidth of the antenna, only one antenna position is necessary.
When only one antenna position is used, the antenna shall be aligned with the middle of the total vehicle.
If the vehicle length is greater than the 3 dB beamwidth of the antenna, multiple antenna positions shall be used to cover the total length of the vehicle.
If N=1, the antenna shall be aligned with the middle of the total vehicle length.
If N>1, the antenna positions shall be symmetric in regard to the vehicle perpendicular axis.
The test method described in Annex 6 shall only be applied to vehicles.
The Annex 6 test method shall apply to vehicle configurations other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid".
The Annex 6 test method shall apply to the "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" vehicle configuration.
The vehicle shall be subjected to electromagnetic fields as described in Annex 6 of UN R10.
The vehicle shall be monitored during the immunity tests.
Unless otherwise stated in Annex 6, the regular immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE.
For vehicles not considered as “large vehicles”, the test shall be performed with front irradiation.
For “large vehicles”, the test shall be performed with front irradiation and with additional antenna positions.

The additional antenna position(s) for large vehicles shall be chosen by the manufacturer in conjunction with the Type-Approval Authority, after considering the distribution of electronic systems with immunity-related functions and the layout of any wiring harness.
The immunity tests shall be performed with the field strength levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of UN R10.
For REESS charging mode, only the electronic systems and wiring harnesses required for charging mode shall be considered when selecting antenna positions.
The immunity test may alternatively be performed in an outdoor test site (OTS) for all vehicles, including large vehicles.
The test facility shall comply with the (national) legal requirements regarding the emission of electromagnetic fields.
The alternative OTS test shall be performed according to ISO 11451-2.
For vehicles not considered as large vehicles, the OTS test shall use front irradiation.
For large vehicles, the OTS test shall use front irradiation together with additional antenna positions.

The additional antenna position(s) for large vehicles shall be chosen by the manufacturer in conjunction with the Type Approval Authority, considering the distribution of electronic systems with immunity related functions and the layout of any wiring harness.
The OTS tests for large vehicles with additional antenna positions shall be performed at the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of this Regulation.
For REESS charging mode, only the electronic systems and wiring harnesses required for charging mode shall be considered when selecting antenna positions.
For large vehicles, the manufacturer may choose one of the following alternative test methods in conjunction with the Type Approval Authority.
Alternative method A: harness excitation (BCI) testing shall be performed according to ISO 11451-4 in the frequency range 20 to 2,000 MHz.
Alternative method A: immunity to external sources shall be tested according to ISO 11451-2 in ALSE or OTS in the frequency range 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, with additional antenna position(s).

In alternative method A, the additional antenna positions shall be chosen by the manufacturer in conjunction with the Type Approval Authority, considering the distribution of electronic systems with immunity related functions and the layout of any wiring harness.
In alternative method B, the ESA involved in immunity related functions shall be chosen by the manufacturer in conjunction with the Type Approval Authority.
Alternative method B: ESA immunity to external sources according to Annex 9 in the frequency range 2,000 to 6,000 MHz shall be tested for all ESA involved in immunity related functions.
In alternative method B, the vehicle test shall be performed at the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of this Regulation.
In alternative method B, the ESA tests shall be performed at the levels defined in paragraph 6.8.2.1. of this Regulation.
Alternative method C: immunity to external sources shall be tested according to ISO 11451-2 in ALSE or OTS in the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz with front irradiation.

Alternative method C: ESA immunity to external sources according to Annex 9 in the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz shall be tested for ESA with immunity related functions outside the antenna beamwidth.
In alternative method C, the concerned ESA shall be chosen by the manufacturer in conjunction with the Type Approval Authority.
In alternative method C, the ESA tests shall be performed at the levels defined in paragraph 6.8.2.1. of this Regulation.
When the alternative method using ESA immunity to external sources according to Annex 9 is used, the concerned ESA shall not require E-marking.
The test report for the ESA immunity test shall be prepared or approved by a laboratory accredited to ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority responsible for carrying out the tests.
The test report for the ESA immunity test shall be provided along with the information document shown in Annex 2B.

The same test method (vehicle type approval in combination with ESA test report for Annex 9) shall be applied during the Conformity of Production test or any applicable test method according to this Annex.
For two-wheeled vehicles tested under UN R10, a non-conductive insulating support with a thickness of 5 to 20 mm shall be used between the stand and the ground plane.
The vehicle shall be in an unladen condition, except for necessary test equipment, during the test.
The engine shall normally turn the driving wheels at a steady speed of 50 km/h, unless there is a technical reason due to the vehicle to define a different condition.

The vehicle shall be on an appropriately loaded dynamometer.
If no dynamometer is available, the vehicle shall alternatively be supported on insulated axle stands with minimum ground clearance.
Where appropriate, transmission shafts, belts or chains may be disconnected (e.g. for trucks, two- and three-wheel vehicles).
All equipment that can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger should be in normal operation.
All other systems which affect the driver's control of the vehicle shall be (on) as in normal operation of the vehicle.

If the vehicle is equipped with an ADS, the immunity test shall demonstrate that the vehicle stays in a failure safe mode or expected failure operational mode during the test in 50 km/h mode or Brake mode.

Additional test run(s) may be necessary to cover untested function(s) (e.g. turn lamp, wiper, etc).
Lateral and longitudinal vehicle motion control and braking may be deactivated if necessary to ensure a safe test environment.

If the vehicle is equipped with an AECS according to UN Regulation No. 144, the AECS shall be tested over the air for transmission of the Minimum Set of Data (MSD) and voice call via a real PLMN or a network simulator, before and after 50 km/h or brake mode, using a private safety answering point (PSAP).
In case of a voice call via a real PLMN, the emergency call number should be changed to a dedicated PSAP number to avoid false calls to the emergency services.
Only one specific cellular configuration, including one frequency band and one channel within a single cellular technology (e.g. 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G), shall be tested.
The vehicle manufacturer and the Technical Service shall review the AECS warning signal strategy if it will detect AECS system faults even when there is no network coverage.
If it is not possible to distinguish between lack of network coverage and an AECS system fault, alternative arrangements shall be made to enable this distinction.

Where a vehicle electrical/electronic system forms an integral part of the immunity related functions but will not operate under the conditions described in paragraph 2.1., the manufacturer may provide a report or additional evidence to the Technical Service that this system meets the requirements of this Regulation.

The report or additional evidence provided to the Technical Service to show that an integral immunity-related electrical/electronic system meets the requirements of this Regulation shall be retained in the type approval documentation.
While monitoring the vehicle, only non-perturbing equipment shall be used.
The vehicle exterior and the passenger compartment shall be monitored to determine whether the requirements of Annex 6 are met.
The vehicle shall be in an unladen condition, except for necessary test equipment.

The engine(s) (ICE and/or electrical engine) shall be OFF and in charging mode.

The REESS shall be in charging mode during the vehicle immunity test.
The REESS State of charge (SOC) shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole frequency range measurement.

For AC charging, if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value.

The vehicle shall not set in motion during the immunity test (failure criterion).
The parking brake shall not be released unexpectedly during the immunity test (failure criterion).
The automatic transmission shall not lose the Parking position during the immunity test (failure criterion).
In case of multiple REESS batteries, the average state of charge shall be considered.
All equipment other than that under test which can be switched ON by the driver or passengers shall be in the OFF state.
While monitoring the vehicle, only non-perturbing equipment shall be used.
The vehicle exterior and the passenger compartment shall be monitored to determine whether the requirements of this Annex are met.
The power mains socket may be placed anywhere in the test site, subject to the conditions listed in this paragraph.
The power mains socket(s) shall be placed on the ground plane (ALSE) or on the floor (OTS).
The length of the harness between the power mains socket and the AMN(s) shall be kept as short as possible, and it need not be aligned with the charging harness.
The harness shall be placed as close as possible to the ground plane (ALSE) or to the floor (OTS).
Power mains shall be applied to the vehicle through 50 µH/50 Ω artificial networks (AMN(s)) during the test.
The AMN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane (ALSE) or on the floor (OTS).
The case of the AMN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane (ALSE) or connected to the protective earth (OTS, e.g. an earth rod).
The measuring port of each AMN shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.

The power charging harness shall be routed perpendicularly to the vehicle longitudinal axis.
The projected harness length from the side of the AMN(s) to the side of the vehicle shall be 0,8 (+0,2 / -0) m.
For a longer cable, the extraneous length of the power charging harness shall be Z-folded symmetrically.
No contact or overlap shall be allowed between the windings of the Z-folded cable.
The width of the Z-folded cable shall be between 500 mm and 1 000 mm.

If it is impractical to Z-fold the extraneous cable length because of cable bulk or stiffness, or because the testing is being done at a user's installation, the disposition of the excess cable length shall be precisely noted in the test report.
The charging harness at the vehicle side shall hang vertically at a distance of 100 (+200 / -0) mm from the vehicle body.
The whole harness shall be placed on a non-conductive, low relative permittivity (dielectric-constant) material with εr ≤ 1,4.
The whole harness shall be placed at (100 ± 25) mm above the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS).
The charging station may be placed either inside the test site or outside the test site.
If the local/private communication between the vehicle and the charging station can be simulated, the charging station may be replaced by a supply from the AC power mains network.

If the charging station is placed inside the test site, the harness at charging station side shall hang vertically down to the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS).
If the charging station is placed inside the test site, the extraneous length of the harness shall be placed as close as possible to the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS) and Z-folded if necessary.

If it is impractical to place the excess cable as close as possible to the ground plane or floor and Z-fold it because of cable bulk or stiffness, or because the testing is done at a user installation, the disposition of the excess cable shall be precisely noted in the test report.

Local/private communication lines connected to signal/control ports and lines connected to wired network ports shall be applied to the vehicle through AAN(s).

For a signal/control port with symmetric lines, the AAN shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.1.
For a wired network port with PLC on power lines, the AAN shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.2.
For a signal/control port with PLC (technology) on control pilot, the AAN shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.3.
For a signal/control port with control pilot, the AAN shall be as defined in Appendix 8, paragraph 5.4.
The AAN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The case of the AAN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane (ALSE) or connected to the protective earth (OTS, e.g. an earth rod).
The measuring port of each AAN shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
If a charging station is used, AAN(s) are not required for the signal/control ports and/or for the wired network ports.
The local/private communication lines between the vehicle and the charging station shall be connected to the auxiliary equipment on the charging station side to work as designed.
If communication is emulated and the presence of the AAN prevents proper communication, no AAN should be used.
The power charging local/private communication harness shall be laid out in a straight line between the AMN(s) / DC-charging-AN(s) / AAN(s) and the vehicle charging socket.

The whole harness shall be placed on a non-conductive, low relative permittivity (dielectric-constant) material with εr ≤ 1,4.
The whole harness shall be placed at (100 ± 25) mm above the ground plane (ALSE) or floor (OTS).

The subject to which this paragraph applies (not named in the paragraph) shall be located at least 2 m horizontally from the antenna phase centre or at least 1 m vertically from the radiating elements of a transmission-line system (TLS).

The test signal modulation specified in items (a) to (c) may differ from those values only if otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the vehicle manufacturer.
The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11451-1.
The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in ISO 11451-1 throughout the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz.

If the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may choose a reduced number of spot frequencies in the range (e.g. 27, 45, 65, 90, 120, 150, 190, 230, 280, 380, 450, 600, 750, 900, 1,300, 1,800, 2,360, 2,600, 3,000, 3,600, 5,200 and 5,900 MHz) to confirm that the vehicle meets the requirements of this Annex.

For antenna calibration, four field probes at the vehicle reference line shall be used.

If the test is not performed with a REESS, the ESA should be tested at rated current.
If the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 80 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.

For ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the test arrangement shall be according to Figure 2 of the appendix to this Annex.

The requirements contained in sections 5 (General specifications) and 6 (Individual specifications) of this Regulation, and in the Annexes referenced in those sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflecting device under this Regulation.

The requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the vehicle category/ies on which the device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The means of attachment of the retro-reflective marking materials shall be durable and stable.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough.
Any protuberances that retro-reflective devices may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning of the outer surface.
When the retro-reflectors are in normal use, there shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors.
A retro-reflector may be constructed as a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter.
The combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter of a retro-reflector shall be designed so that the two cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
Retro-reflecting optical units and filters shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
The night-time colour test specifications of this section shall apply only to white, red or amber retro-reflective devices.
When testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A.
When testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the illumination shall have an angle of divergence of 1/3°.
When testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the illumination angle shall be β1 = β2 = 0°.

If the illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1 shall be used instead when testing the colour of the retro-reflective device.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflective device shall be within the night-time colour limits for the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.

White retro-reflective devices must not produce selective reflection, defined as the trichromatic coordinates "x" and "y" of Standard Illuminant "A" used to illuminate the retro-reflective device changing by more than 0.01 after reflection by the retro-reflective device.
For daytime colour testing, the material shall be illuminated by the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006).
For daytime colour testing, the illumination geometry shall be (45a:0) or (0:45a), as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
For the determination of the luminance factor, the sample shall be tested with the method described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6.

At least one hour after the heat resistance test, the ten samples shall be examined for colorimetric characteristics (paragraph 5.1.5.) and RI (paragraph 5.1.4.) at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values shall then be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
The two samples giving the minimum and maximum values shall be kept by the laboratories for any further checks which may be found necessary.
Four samples out of the remaining eight samples shall be selected at random and divided into two groups of two samples each.
The other eight samples shall be divided into four groups of two samples each (first, second, third and fourth groups).
The two samples of the first group shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6).
If the water penetration test of the first group is satisfactory, the two samples shall then be subjected to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
If necessary, the two samples of the second group shall be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6.
The two samples of the second group shall then be subjected to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The two samples of the third group shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of the retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The two samples of the fourth group shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each group must have the properties listed in the enumeration that follows this paragraph.

For a retro-reflector (RI) that satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., the verification shall be performed only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°.
