Retro-reflective devices and fluorescent retro-reflecting material shall have a coefficient of retro-reflection (RI) not less than the minimum values in Table 8 for each illumination angle (β1 vertical, β2 horizontal) and each angle of divergence.

At an angle of divergence of 20', the RI of retro-reflective devices and fluorescent retro-reflecting material shall be at least 8.00∙10³ mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 0° and β2 0° or ±5°, 4.00∙10³ mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 ±20° and β2 0°, 1.70∙10³ mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 0° and β2 ±30°, and 6.00∙10² mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 0° and β2 ±40°.

At an angle of divergence of 1°30', the RI of retro-reflective devices and fluorescent retro-reflecting material shall be at least 6.00∙10² mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 0° and β2 0° or ±5°, 2.00∙10² mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 ±20° and β2 0°, 1.00∙10² mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 0° and β2 ±30°, and 5.0∙10¹ mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 0° and β2 ±40°.

The RI measured on random slices of 50 mm length of the retro-reflective device, at a divergence angle of 20' and at illumination angles β1 = 0°, β2 = 0° or ±5° and β1 = ±20°, β2 = 0°, shall lie between extremes having a ratio not exceeding 3.

The random 50 mm slices of the retro-reflective device used for the RI measurement shall be taken between the perpendiculars to the side of the triangle passing through the corresponding apexes of the central aperture.

Diversity of luminance at illumination angles V β1 = 0°, H β2 = ±30°, and β1 = 0°, β2 = ±40° is tolerated only on condition that the triangular shape remains clearly discernible, for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination of approximately 1 lux.
The retro-reflection measurements referred to above shall be performed by the method described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
Retro-reflective devices of the advance warning triangle shall be made of material coloured red in the mass.
The colour testing of the retro-reflective device (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.

The trichromatic co-ordinates of the red reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflective device (night-time colour) shall be within the limits in Table 9: point 1 (x 0.712, y 0.258), point 2 (x 0.735, y 0.265), point 3 (x 0.589, y 0.376), point 4 (x 0.625, y 0.375).
The fluorescent materials of the advance warning triangle shall either be coloured in the mass or take the form of separate coatings applied to the surface of the triangle.
The testing of the colour of the fluorescent materials (daytime colour) of advance warning triangle type 1 or type 2 shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.2.

The colour of the fluorescent material (daytime colour) of advance warning triangle type 1 or type 2 in new condition shall be within an area whose corner points are at the Table 10 chromaticity coordinates: point 1 (x 0.570, y 0.430), point 2 (x 0.506, y 0.404), point 3 (x 0.595, y 0.315), point 4 (x 0.690, y 0.310).
The testing of the luminance factor of the fluorescent materials of advance warning triangles shall be carried out according to the method described in Part 6 of Annex 6.
For an advance warning triangle of type 1, the luminance factor βv,R, including the luminance by reflection and fluorescence, shall be ≥ 0.3.
For an advance warning triangle of type 2, the luminance factor βv,R, including the luminance by reflection and fluorescence, shall be ≥ 0.25.

The largest measured trichromatic coordinate y value of the night-time colour, determined according to paragraph 4.2.1., shall be smaller than or equal to the largest measured trichromatic coordinate y value of the daytime colour, determined according to paragraph 4.2.2.
After weathering, when tested according to Part 6 of Annex 6, the advance warning triangle shall fulfil the conditions listed in the following paragraphs.
After the weathering test, the colour co-ordinates of the fluorescent material of the advance warning triangle shall comply with the colour specification in paragraph 5.3.5.2.2.
After the weathering test, the luminance factor of the advance warning triangle, determined as defined in paragraph 4.3., shall comply with the luminance factor requirement in paragraph 5.3.5.2.3.
After the weathering test, the luminance factor of the advance warning triangle shall not have increased by more than 0.05 relative to its value before the test.
After weathering, the sample shall not exhibit any visible damage such as cracks, scaling or peeling of the fluorescent material or of the fluorescent retro-reflecting material.
If the fluorescent material is an adhesive film that has already successfully passed the tests of paragraph 5.3.7.1.7. in a previous approval test, the weathering test need not be repeated.

When the tests of paragraph 5.3.7.1.7. are not repeated because the adhesive fluorescent film already passed them in a previous approval test, a corresponding note shall be entered under item 9 ("Remarks") in the communication concerning approval (Annex 1).
A specimen of the advance warning triangle shall be subjected to the resistance-to-weathering test specified in Part 6 of Annex 6.
A specimen of the sample unit of the advance warning triangle shall be subjected to the resistance-to-fuels test specified in Part 1 of Annex 7.
A specimen of the sample unit of the advance warning triangle shall be subjected to the resistance to heat test specified in Annex 9.
A specimen of the sample unit of the advance warning triangle shall be subjected to the resistance-to-penetration-of-water test specified in Part 2 of Annex 6.
A specimen of a complete plate shall be subjected to a test of rigidity of plates as specified in Annex 9.
A specimen of the sample unit of the advance warning triangle shall be subjected to the clearance to ground test as specified in Annex 9.
The applicant shall submit samples, as mentioned in paragraph 3.1., for approval.

After verification of the general specifications in paragraph 4. and the shape and dimensions specified in Figure A5-VIII or Figure A5-IX, all samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test in Annex 9.
After the heat resistance test in Annex 9, all samples shall be examined after at least one hour of rest.
The RI value of the four submitted advance warning triangle samples shall be measured at an observation angle of 20' and at an illumination angle with the components β1 = 0° and β2 = ± 5°.
The RI measurement of the advance warning triangle samples shall be carried out in accordance with the method described in paragraph 4 of the regulation.
The two samples with the smallest and the largest RI value in the tests according to paragraph 5.9.7.1.3 shall be subsequently subjected to the following tests.
The colour of the retro-reflected light, tested according to paragraph 4.2., shall be examined on the sample with the highest RI concerned.
One sample other than those referred to in paragraph 5.3.7.1.4 shall be subjected to the following tests.
The second sample, other than the samples referred to in paragraph 5.3.7.1.4., shall be subjected to the tests listed following this paragraph.
After the tests specified in paragraph 5.3.7.1.4. are completed, the two samples submitted according to paragraph 3.1. shall be subjected to the following tests.

After the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6), the colour co-ordinates of the fluorescent material of the advance warning triangle shall comply with the colour specification in paragraph 5.3.5.2.2. of this Regulation.

After the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6), the luminance factor of the fluorescent material of the advance warning triangle, as defined in paragraph 4.3., shall comply with paragraph 5.3.5.2.3. of this Regulation.

After the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6), the luminance factor of the fluorescent material of the advance warning triangle shall not have increased by more than 5 per cent compared with the value ascertained according to paragraph 5.3.7.1.7.2.

After the weathering resistance test according to Part 6 of Annex 6, the sample shall not exhibit any visible damage such as cracks, scaling or peeling of the fluorescent or of the fluorescent retro-reflecting material.
If the fluorescent material is an adhesive film that had already successfully passed the tests of paragraph 5.3.7.1.7. in a previous approval test, the test need not be repeated.

Where the test is not repeated because the adhesive film already passed the tests of paragraph 5.3.7.1.7. in a previous approval test, a corresponding note shall be entered under item 9 ("Remarks") in the communication concerning approval (Annex 1 to this Regulation).

To verify that a device approved under a preceding series of amendments is not affected by the latest changes, the change index applicable to the pertinent device shall not differ from its change index as indicated in the latest series of amendments.
Contracting Parties applying UN R150 shall not refuse to grant extensions to type approvals according to any preceding series of amendments to UN R150.

From the official date of entry into force of the 01 series of amendments, no Contracting Party applying UN R150 shall refuse to grant or refuse to accept UN type approvals under UN R150 as amended by the 01 series of amendments.

Contracting Parties applying UN R150 shall continue to grant and accept type approvals for devices (equipment and parts) on the basis of any previous series of amendments, provided that the devices are intended as replacements for fitting to vehicles in use and that it is not technically feasible for those devices to satisfy the new requirements of UN R150 as amended by the 01 series of amendments.

The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices with respect to photometric performance shall not be contested if, when the photometric performance of any randomly chosen retro-reflective device is tested, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with.
For each type of retro-reflective device, the holder of the approval mark shall carry out at least the following tests at appropriate intervals.
The tests carried out by the holder of the approval mark for conformity of production shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of UN R150.
If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested.
The manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
Tests of conformity under UN R150 shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.
Tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in UN R150.
In any test of conformity carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used only with the consent of the Type Approval Authority.
The manufacturer shall prove that any alternative test methods applied in a conformity test are equivalent to those laid down in UN R150.
In all cases, the reference methods used for administrative verification and sampling shall be those specified in this Regulation.
Samples of retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch.
The assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories.
A manufacturer may group together records concerning the same type from several factories, provided these factories operate under the same quality system and quality management.
The sampled retro-reflective device shall be subjected to photometric measurements at the points and the chromaticity coordinates provided for in the Regulation.
The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results.

The manufacturer shall define, in agreement with the Type Approval Authority, criteria governing the acceptability of its products so as to meet the specifications laid down for the verification of conformity of products in paragraph 3.5.1. of this Regulation.
The acceptability criteria shall be such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 3 (first sampling) would be 0.95.

The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, provided the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices with respect to photometric performance shall not be contested when photometric performance testing of any randomly chosen retro-reflective device meets the conditions that follow in the listed requirements.
No measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in UN R150.
The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with (the applicable chromaticity limits are defined elsewhere in the regulation; this paragraph does not state them).
The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four retro-reflective devices) is not more than 20 per cent.
If the deviation of both retro-reflective devices of sample A is not more than 0 per cent, the measurement may be closed.
The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent.
Where conformity is contested, the manufacturer shall be requested to bring his mass production in line with the requirements (alignment).
A repeated sampling according to paragraph 3 shall be carried out within two months after the notification to the manufacturer.
The Technical Service shall retain samples A and B until the entire CoP process is finished.
The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples C and D (all four retro-reflective devices) is not more than 20 per cent.
If the deviation of both retro-reflective devices of sample C is not more than 0 per cent, the measurement may be closed.
The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested if the deviation of at least the parameters listed in the enumeration that follows this paragraph is found.

Where one specimen of sample C or D is more than 20 per cent deviant but the deviation of all specimens of these samples is not more than 30 per cent, the manufacturer shall be requested again to bring his production in line with the requirements (alignment).

Where one specimen of sample C or D is more than 20 per cent deviant but the deviation of all specimens of these samples is not more than 30 per cent, a second repeated sampling according to paragraph 4. shall be carried out within two months' time after the notification.
Samples C and D shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire CoP process is finished.
If one specimen of samples C and D is more than 30 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn.
If one specimen of samples C and D is more than 30 per cent, paragraph 5 shall be applied.
The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples E and F (all four retro-reflective devices) is not more than 20 per cent.
The measurement of mass-produced retro-reflective devices may be closed if the deviation of both retro-reflective devices of sample E is not more than 0 per cent.
The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent.
Where conformity is contested because the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F of mass-produced retro-reflective devices is more than 20 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn.
Where conformity is contested because the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F of mass-produced retro-reflective devices is more than 20 per cent, paragraph 5 shall be applied.
Approval shall be withdrawn according to paragraph 3.6. of UN R150.
After the sampling procedure in paragraph 2, one of the retro-reflectors of sample A shall be tested according to the procedure described in paragraph 1 of Part 2 of Annex 6.
For the Advance Warning Triangle, sample A shall be tested according to the procedure described in paragraph 2 of Part 2 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflectors shall be considered acceptable if the test has been passed.
If the test on sample A is not complied with, the two retro-reflective devices of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure.
Both retro-reflective devices of sample B shall pass the test.
After the sampling procedure in paragraph 2., specimens of one of the rear marking plates of sample A shall be tested.
The specimens of one rear marking plate of sample A shall be tested according to the procedures described in Annexes 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 16 and 18 to UN R150.
The rear marking plate of sample A shall be considered acceptable only if it passes the tests.
If the tests on specimens of sample A did not pass, the two rear marking plates of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure.
If the tests on specimens of sample A did not pass, both rear marking plates of sample B shall pass the test.
When the RI of a retro-reflective device is measured at an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device.
If a mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the retro-reflective device, a reading of its RI shall be taken at an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5.) and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI.
The minimum RI of a retro-reflective device, found by rotating it about its axis of reference, must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.
When the RI is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the value of ε at which minimum RI was found.
If the specified values are not attained, the retro-reflective device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from the minimum RI position.

When the illumination angle β is β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation) and the angle of divergence is 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°.
The RI of a retro-reflective device marked "TOP" shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during the ±5° rotation about its axes.
If, for the direction β1 = β2 = 0° and for ε = 0°, the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
The CIE-angular system shown in Figure A4-I shall be used for specifying and measuring retro-reflective devices and marking materials.

When testing retro-reflection, the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
During photometric measurements, stray reflections should be avoided by appropriate masking.
The measuring distance shall be chosen so that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η given above and illustrated in Figure A4-III are respected.
The measuring distance shall not be lower than 10 m.
The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform.
The measuring element used to check the illuminance uniformity shall have a sensitive area not greater than one-tenth of the area to be examined.
The variation in the value of the illuminance over the useful area shall comply with the condition max/min ≤ 1.05.
The photometer head shall be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency for the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.
The device shall not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture.

If the device would show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture, suitable provisions shall be added to the device, e.g. the application of a diffusing window at a certain distance in front of the sensitive surface.
The background to the sample and the framework of the sample holder should be matt black.
The field of view of the photometer head shall be restricted as much as possible.
The spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.
Reflections from the floor and walls that occur over the relatively long test distances used shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.

Correction of residual stray light should be allowed for by measuring it when the sample is covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape, or a specular black surface suitably oriented with a light trap.
The residual stray light value measured with the sample covered shall be subtracted from the value measured on the retro-reflective device.
The light source and photometer head shall remain stable throughout the period of the test.
The laboratory ambient temperature shall not vary significantly during the period of the test.
Sufficient time shall always be allowed for the apparatus to stabilize before commencing measurements.

When testing the daytime colour and luminance factor of retro-reflective material, the material shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0).
Daytime colour measurements shall be performed with a spectrophotometer in accordance with CIE Publication 15:2004, Recommendations on Colorimetry - Second Edition.
The daytime colour measurement shall illuminate the sample at an angle of 45° to the normal and view it along the normal (geometry 45/0).
Where a monochromator providing stepwise CIE Standard Illuminant D65 is used, the stepwise resolution Δλ shall not be larger than 10 nm.
Similar simulation spectra in place of CIE D65 may be used only if it is verified that the colorimetric measuring procedure is of the same accuracy.
The quality of the D65 simulation shall be assessed by the method described in ISO 23603:2005(E)/CIE S 012/E:2004.
The spectral distribution of the illuminant shall be in category BC (CIELAB) or better.
The measurement area shall be at least 4.0 cm².
For micro-prismatic materials showing flares or sparkles, special precautions as outlined in the measurement procedure shall be taken to avoid influence on the measured results.

For the 45/0 geometry, the sampling aperture should be irradiated uniformly from all directions between two circular cones whose axes are normal to the sampling aperture and whose apices are at the centre of the sampling aperture.
Of the two illumination cones, the smaller shall have a half angle of 40° and the larger a half angle of 50°.
The receiver should uniformly collect and evaluate all radiation reflected within a cone whose axis is on the normal to the sampling aperture and whose apex is at the centre of the sampling aperture.
The collection cone of the receiver should have a half angle of 5°.
The annular illumination geometry may be approximated by a number of light sources arranged in a ring, or by a number of fibre bundles illuminated by a single source and terminated in a ring.
As an alternative approximation, a single light source may be used with the sample rotated during measurement.

When the sample is rotated with a single light source, the rotational speed shall ensure that a number of revolutions takes place during the exposure time interval of a measurement so that all circumferential angles are given equal weight.
The apertures of the light source and the receiver shall have sufficient dimensions in proportion to the distances to ensure compliance with the geometry recommendations.
The Type Approval Authorities of Contracting Parties in which the approval was granted may undertake the same tests.
If "systematic failures in use" occur for a type of retro-reflective material, the tested material samples of that type shall be transferred for appraisal to the authority which granted approval.
The authority which granted approval shall have the right to check the stability in time of the optical properties of a type of rear marking plate in service.
Type Approval Authorities of countries other than the country in which approval was granted may carry out similar checks in their territory.

If a type of rear marking plate in use exhibits a systematic defect, the Type Approval Authorities of countries other than the country in which approval was granted shall transmit to the authority which granted approval, with a request for its opinion, any components removed for examination.
In the absence of other criteria, the concept of "systematic defect" of a type of rear marking plate in use shall be interpreted in conformity with the intention of paragraph 5. of Part 3 of Annex 4.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors in paragraph 2.1., when observed from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The illuminating surfaces of retro-reflective devices of Classes IIIA and IIIB must have the shape of an equilateral triangle.
If the word "TOP" is inscribed in one corner of the illuminating surface of a retro-reflective device of Class IIIA or IIIB, the apex of that corner must be directed upwards.
The illuminating surface may or may not have, at its centre, a triangular non-retro-reflecting area.
If the illuminating surface has a triangular non-retro-reflecting area at its centre, the sides of that area shall be parallel to those of the outer triangle.
The illuminating surface may be continuous or may be non-continuous.
The shortest distance between two adjacent retro-reflecting optical units must not exceed 15 mm.

The illuminating surface of a retro-reflective device is considered continuous only if the edges of the illuminating surfaces of adjacent separate optical units are parallel and the said optical units are evenly distributed over the whole solid surface of the triangle.

If the illuminated surface of the retro-reflector is not continuous, the number of separate retro-reflecting optical units, including the corner units, shall be not less than four on each side of the triangle.
The separate retro-reflecting optical units shall not be replaceable, unless they consist of approved retro-reflective devices of Class IA.
The outside edges of the illuminating surfaces of triangular retro-reflective devices of Classes IIIA and IIIB shall be between 150 and 200 mm long.

In hollow-triangle type triangular retro-reflective devices of Classes IIIA and IIIB, the width of the sides, measured at right angles to the outside edges, shall be equal to at least 20 per cent of the effective length between the extremities of the illuminating surface.
From an observation distance of 10 metres, the shape of the light emitting surfaces shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors in paragraph 2.1.
The light emitting surface of the retro-reflective device must be at least 25 cm2.
Compliance with the specifications above in Annex 5 of UN R150 shall be verified by visual inspection.
The markings shall be made of strips of retro-reflective material.
The width of a retro-reflective marking material shall be 50 mm +10/-0 mm.
The minimum length of an element of a retro-reflective marking material shall be such that at least one approval mark is visible.
The markings shall be made of strips of retro-reflective material or plates.
Class F and Class 5 retro-reflective markings shall consist of red and white diagonal stripes running downwards at 45° ± 1°, as shown in Figures A5-II, A5-III and A5-IV respectively.
The basic standard area shall be a square of 141 mm ± 1 mm in length.
The basic standard area shall be subdivided diagonally into a white half and a red half.

The minimum length of an element of a retro-reflective marking material or plate shall incorporate a minimum of 9 standard areas as described in paragraph 5.2.1 on large vehicles with available mounting space.
On vehicles with limited mounting space, the minimum length of an element of a retro-reflective marking material or plate may be reduced to a minimum of 3 standard areas.
The plates shall be rectangular in shape for mounting at the rear of vehicles.
For plates mounted on trailers and semi-trailers, the plate shall have a yellow retro-reflective background with a red fluorescent or retro-reflective border.

For plates mounted on non-articulated vehicles (tractors or trucks), the plate shall be of the chevron type with alternate oblique stripes of yellow retro-reflective and red fluorescent or retro-reflective materials or devices.
The minimum total summarized length of a set of rear marking plates consisting only of one, two or four marking plates with retro-reflective and fluorescent materials shall be 1,130 mm.
The maximum total length of a set of rear marking plates consisting only of one, two or four marking plates with retro-reflective and fluorescent materials shall be 2,300 mm.
The width of a rear marking plate on trucks and tractors shall be 140 ± 10 mm.
The width of a rear marking plate on trailers and semi‑trailers shall be 200 +30/-5 mm.

The length of each rear marking plate in a set of two plates for trucks and tractors (as illustrated in Figures A5-V and A5-VI) may be reduced to a minimum of 130 mm, provided that the width is increased.
Each marking on a rear marking plate in the two-plate set for trucks and tractors, where the length has been reduced, shall have an area of at least 735 cm2.
Each marking on a rear marking plate in the two-plate set for trucks and tractors, where the length has been reduced, shall not exceed an area of 1,725 cm2.
The marking plates in the two-plate set for trucks and tractors, where the length has been reduced, shall be rectangular.
The width of the red fluorescent border of the rear marking plates for trailers and semi-trailers shall be 40 mm ± 1 mm.
The slope of the oblique stripes of the chevron band shall be 45º ± 5º.
The width of the stripes of the chevron band shall be 100 mm ± 2.5 mm.
Rear marking plates supplied in sets shall form matching pairs.
The plates shall be in the shape of an equilateral triangle with truncated corners.
The plates shall be mounted with one apex upwards at the rear of slow-moving vehicles.
The SMV rear marking plates shall have a red fluorescent centre.
The SMV rear marking plates (class 1) shall have red retro-reflective borders made of either retro-reflective material or coating or of plastic corner-cube reflectors.
The SMV rear marking plates of class 2 shall have a retro-reflective centre.
The length of the base of the enclosed fluorescent triangle (class 1) or retro-reflective triangle (class 2) shall be at least 350 mm and at most 365 mm.
The minimum width of the light-emitting surface of the red retro-reflective border shall be 45 mm.
The maximum width of the light-emitting surface of the red retro-reflective border shall be 48 mm.
The theoretical sides of the triangle shall be 500 ± 50 mm long.
For an advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflecting units shall be arranged along the edge within a strip of an unvarying width between 25 mm and 50 mm.
For an advance warning triangle of type 2 with fluorescent retro-reflecting material, the unvarying width of the strip shall be between 50 mm and 85 mm.
Between the outer edge of the triangle and the retro-reflecting strip, an edging may be present only if it is not more than 5 mm wide.
The edging between the outer edge of the triangle and the retro-reflecting strip need not be red-coloured.
The retro-reflecting strip may be either continuous or non-continuous.
Where the retro-reflecting strip is not continuous, the free area of the supporting material shall be red.
For an advance warning triangle of type 1, the fluorescent surface shall be continuous to the retro-reflecting units.
For an advance warning triangle of type 1, the fluorescent surface shall be arranged symmetrically along the three sides of the triangle.
For an advance warning triangle of type 1, when in use, the surface area of the fluorescent surface shall be not less than 315 cm2.

For an advance warning triangle of type 1, an edging, continuous or not, not more than 5 mm wide, which need not necessarily be red-coloured, may be placed between the retro-reflecting surface and the fluorescent surface.
The side of the open centre of the triangle shall have a minimum length of 70 mm.
The distance between the supporting surface and the lower side of the advance warning triangle shall not exceed 300 mm.
The fluorescent retro-reflecting material shall be coloured in the mass, either in the retro-reflective elements or as a solid surface layer.

For the moulded plastics reflector test of retro-reflecting devices (Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle type 1), the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C.
After the 48-hour dry heat conditioning at 65 °C ± 2 °C, the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.

A section of a sample unit, not less than 300 mm long, shall be kept for 12 hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 ºC (flexible materials for Classes C, D, E, F, marking plates of Classes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and advance warning triangle of type 2).
After the 65 °C heating step, the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 ºC.
After the cooling step, the sample shall be kept for 12 hours at −20 °C ± 2 ºC.
The sample shall be examined after a recovery time of 4 hours under normal laboratory conditions.
After the test, the retro-reflective device, and in particular its optical component, shall show no cracking or appreciable distortion visible to the eye.
Retro-reflective devices (whether part of a lamp or not) or sample units of retro-reflective marking shall be stripped of all removable parts before the immersion test.
Retro-reflective devices or sample units shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C.
During the 50 °C immersion, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface shall be 20 mm below the surface of the water.
The 50 °C immersion test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°.
In the repeated test, the illuminating surface shall be at the bottom so that the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
After the 50 °C test, the sample units shall then be immediately immersed under the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
Water shall not penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water on the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
For retro-reflectors, the RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
For retro-reflectors, the retro-reflective device shall first be lightly shaken to remove excess water from its outside before the RI is measured.
For a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, the coefficient of retro-reflection R' shall be measured in conformity with Part 2 of Annex 6.
For a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, the sample unit shall first be lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside before R' is measured.
The triangle, assembled as for use, shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water having a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C.
During the 50 °C immersion, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface of the triangle shall be about 20 mm below the water surface.

Immediately after the 50 °C immersion, the retro-reflective device shall be immersed under the same conditions (10 minutes, highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface about 20 mm below the water surface) in water having a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
After the test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflective device.
If a visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall be deemed to have failed the test.
Water or water vapour penetration into the edges of fluorescent retro-reflecting materials shall not be deemed to indicate failure.

If the visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water, or in case of doubt, the value of the RI shall again be measured under the same conditions as specified in paragraph 1.2. of Part 2 of Annex 6, after the retro-reflective device has been gently shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
The RI shall not have diminished by more than 40 per cent of the values recorded before the test.
A collapsible advance warning triangle, assembled as for use, shall be immersed flat for two hours on the bottom of a tank containing water at 25 °C ± 5 °C during the water test.
During the water immersion test, the active face of the triangle shall face upwards and be 5 cm under the surface of the water.
After the water immersion, the triangle shall be removed from the tank and dried.
No part of the triangle shall exhibit clear signs of deterioration that might impair the effectiveness of the triangle after the water test.
A section of a sample unit not less than 300 mm long shall be immersed in distilled water at a temperature of 23 ± 5 ºC for a period of 18 hours.
After immersion, the section shall be left to dry for 24 hours under normal laboratory conditions.
After completion of the test, the section shall be examined.
No part inside 10 mm from the cut edge of the section shall show evidence of deterioration which would reduce the effectiveness of the plate.
As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests shall be applied.
A water spray cabinet with the characteristics listed in the following paragraphs shall be used as the water spray test equipment.
The cabinet shall be equipped with a nozzle(s) that provides a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device.
The centreline of the nozzle(s) shall be directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of a rotating test platform.
The rotating test platform shall have a minimum diameter of 140 mm.
The rotating test platform shall rotate about a vertical axis in the centre of the cabinet.
The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min.
The precipitation rate at the device shall be measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform.
The height of the vertical cylindrical precipitation collector shall be 100 mm.
The inside diameter of the precipitation collector shall be a minimum of 140 mm.
A sample device mounted on a test fixture, with its initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to a water spray in the water spray test procedure.
All drain holes and other openings in the device shall remain open.
When drain wicks are used, they shall be tested in the device.
The device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min -1 during the rotational speed test.

When the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, those signalling or lighting functions shall be operated at design voltage in a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode where appropriate) and 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours, consisting of 12 cycles of 5/55 min.
During the drain period, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF.
The device shall be allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.
Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation.
No standing pool of water shall be formed in the device, including any pool that can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
The RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, after the exterior of the device has been dried with a dry cotton cloth.
The equipment listed after this paragraph shall be used to test for dust exposure. (The list itself is not included in this paragraph.)
The interior of the dust exposure test chamber shall be cubical in shape, with each side between 0.9 m and 1.5 m.
The bottom of the dust exposure test chamber may be hopper shaped to aid in collecting the dust.
The internal volume of the dust exposure test chamber, excluding a hopper-shaped bottom, shall be 2 m3 maximum.
The dust exposure test chamber shall be charged with 3 to 5 kg of the test dust.
The dust exposure test chamber shall be capable of agitating the test dust by means of compressed air or blower fans, such that the dust is diffused throughout the chamber.
The test dust used shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
A sample device, mounted on a test fixture and with its initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust in the manner specified in the following sub-paragraphs of Annex 6 Part 3 2.3.4.
All drain holes and other openings in the device shall remain open.
When drain wicks are used in the device, they shall be tested in the device.
The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall.
A device with a length exceeding 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.
The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s).
The test dust shall be agitated at intervals of 15 min.
Each agitation of the test dust shall last for a period of 2 to 15 s.
The dust exposure shall be carried out for the duration of 5 hours.
The dust shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.
Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth.
Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

Retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The resistance of the front surface of a retro-reflective device to tarnishing and the protection of its rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.
The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts before the saline mist test.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each.
The two 24-hour saline mist exposure periods shall be separated by an interval of two hours, during which the sample is allowed to dry.
For retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C.

For retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the atomized saline solution shall be obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured after a 48-hour recovery period as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured after a 48-hour recovery period as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not more than the value in Table 10.
Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection, the surface of the retro-reflective areas shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.
The reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, after brushing the rear face of the retro-reflective device, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the rear face for one minute.
After the one-minute application, the cotton cloth shall be removed and the retro-reflective device shall be left to dry.

For moulded plastics reflectors of advance warning triangle type 1, after brushing, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be covered or thoroughly wetted for one minute with the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7.
After the one-minute exposure to the Annex 7 Part 1 mixture, the fuel shall be removed from the retro-reflective device and the device allowed to dry.
As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side shall be brushed with the same brush as before.
The RI shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation only after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
In the case of the retro-reflector of an Advance warning triangle of type 1, the RI shall not have diminished by more than 40 per cent of the values recorded before the test.
The 40 per cent diminishment test on the retro-reflector of an Advance warning triangle of type 1 shall not be applied to fluorescent retro-reflecting material.
The apparatus shall comply with EN ISO 4892-1:2016.
The apparatus shall comply with EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The apparatus shall be capable of controlling temperature and relative humidity.
The apparatus shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system shall be capable of spraying a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² of water within 5 minutes.
The spray water used in the test shall comply with the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The test method used shall be specified in the test report.
The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1.
For fluorescent materials, the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be run for a period of 100 hours.
The temperature sensor that correlates best with the samples should be used (e.g. a Black-Panel thermometer for reflective material applied on aluminium substrate).
Preparation of test specimens shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
Samples should be relocated in the Xenon tester regularly (e.g. 4-8 times per test), in line with good laboratory practice.
In case of dispute, the natural outdoor exposure results shall prevail over the accelerated weathering test results.
The stated ± tolerances for irradiance, black-panel temperature and relative humidity shall not be interpreted as permitting the value to vary by plus/minus the indicated amount from the given value.
A test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol shall be applied for either of the alternatives listed after this paragraph.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device, and in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.
About five minutes after the wiping, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually.
The surface of the retro-reflective device shall not show any apparent surface changes after the test, except that slight surface cracks shall not be objected to.
A section of the retro-reflective marking material sample unit, not less than 300 mm long, shall be immersed in the test mixture for one minute.
After removal from the test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective marking material sample shall be wiped dry with a soft cloth.
After immersion in the test mixture and wiping dry, the surface of the retro-reflective marking material sample shall not show any visible change which would reduce its effective performance.
The warning triangle and its protective cover shall be immersed separately in a tank containing a mixture of 70 per cent n-heptane and 30 per cent toluene.
After 60 seconds of immersion, the triangle and its protective cover shall be removed from the tank and drained of excess liquid.
The triangle shall then be placed in its protective cover, and the unit shall be laid flat in a still atmosphere.
When completely dried, the warning triangle shall not adhere to its protective cover.
When completely dried, there shall be no visually noticeable change on the surface of the triangle.
When completely dried, the triangle shall not present apparent detrimental modifications.
When completely dried, slight surface cracks on the triangle may be tolerated.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device, and in particular its illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.
After about 5 minutes, the surface shall be cleaned.
After the cleaning, the RI shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
A test sample smeared with a mixture of detergent, lubricating oil and graphite shall be easily cleaned without damage to the retro-reflective surface.
The test sample smeared with the detergent/lubricating oil/graphite mixture shall be cleaned by wiping with a mild aliphatic solvent such as n-heptane, followed by washing with a neutral detergent.

When the test component in its normal mounting conditions is subjected to a continuous spraying action for 60 seconds, the test sample shall show no damage to the retro-reflective surface, no delamination from the substrate, and no separation from the sample mounting surface.
The power washing test shall be performed with a water/wash solution pressure of 8 ± 0.2 MPa.
The power washing test shall be performed with a water/wash solution temperature of 60 +0/-5 °C.
The power washing test shall be performed with a water/wash solution flow rate of 7 ± 1 l/min.
The tip of the cleaning wand shall be positioned at a distance of 600 ± 20 mm away from the retro-reflective surface during the power washing test.
The cleaning wand shall be held at an angle of no greater than 45 degrees from perpendicular to the retro-reflective surface during the power washing test.
The power washing test shall be performed using a 40-degree nozzle creating a wide fan pattern.
For retro-reflective marking material, the bonding strength test shall use an aluminium plate as the substrate.
For retro-reflective marking material, the application of the material for the bonding strength test shall be done according to the manufacturer's recommendation.
The adhesion of retro-reflective material shall be determined after 24 hours curing time by utilising a 90-degree peel on a tensile strength testing machine.
The retro-reflective material shall not be easily removable without damaging the material.
The retro-reflective material shall require a force of at least 10 N per 25 mm width, applied at a constant speed of 300 mm per minute, to be removed from its substrate.
A specimen of the sample unit measuring 50 mm by 300 mm shall be bent once lengthwise around a 3.2 mm mandrel, with adhesive contacting the mandrel for a period of 1 second.
The test temperature shall be 23 °C ± 2 °C in UN R150 Annex 8 Part 3.
After the test, the specimen shall not have cracking of its surface.
After the test, the specimen shall not show any visible change that would reduce its effective performance.

For rear marking plates (except plastics corner-cube reflectors), when a 25 mm diameter solid steel ball is dropped from a height of 2 m onto the retro-reflective and fluorescent surfaces of a supported plate at an ambient temperature of 23 ± 2 ºC, the material shall show no cracking or separation from the substrate at a distance of more than 5 mm from the impacted area.
For the Class IVA impact test, the retro-reflective device shall be mounted in a manner similar to how it is mounted on the vehicle, but with the lens faced horizontal and directed upwards.
For the Class IVA impact test, a 13 mm diameter polished solid steel ball shall be dropped once, vertically, onto the central part of the lens from a height of 0.76 m.
The steel ball may be guided during the Class IVA drop test, but its free fall shall not be restricted.
When a Class IVA retro-reflective device is tested at room temperature with the specified drop method, the lens shall not crack.
The rear marking plate shall be placed on two supports that are parallel to the shorter edge of the plate.
The distance from either support to the adjacent edge of the rear marking plate shall not exceed L/10, where L is the greater overall dimension of the plate.
The rear marking plate shall then be loaded with bags of shot or of dry sand to a uniformly distributed pressure of 1.5 kN/m2.
The deflection of the rear marking plate shall be measured at a point midway between the two supports.

When tested as described in paragraph 1.1 of Part 5 of Annex 8, the maximum deflection of the plate under the test load shall not exceed one twentieth of the distance between the supports in paragraph 1.
When tested as described in paragraph 1.1 of Part 5 of Annex 8, the residual deflection of the plate after removal of the test load shall not exceed one fifth of the measured deflection under load.
The triangular plate shall be strongly held on one of its long sides during the test.
The clamps of the holding device shall not encroach over the triangular plate by more than 20 mm.
A force of 10 N, perpendicular to the plane of the triangular plate, shall be applied to the apex opposite the held long side.
Subsequently, the apex shall not move in the direction of the force by more than 40 mm.
After removal of the force, the plate shall visibly return to its initial position.
The residual deflection of the plate after removal of the force shall not be more than 5 mm.
The advance warning triangle shall pass the test specified in the following paragraph of Annex 9.
The test apparatus shown in Figure A5-X, which has the form of an inverted hollow pyramid, shall be placed on a horizontal base plane.
The individual supports to the ground shall be placed one after another in the square hole σ of the test apparatus.

During the test of each support, a position of the test apparatus in relation to the advance warning triangle and its supporting device shall be found that is favourable for the triangle and ensures the conditions listed in the following items (the listed conditions are not included in this paragraph).
Outside the area covered by the test apparatus, the distance between the base plane and any parts of the triangle and of the supporting device shall be at least 50 mm, except for the supports proper.

When the advance warning triangle has been set up as required by the manufacturer and its bases are firmly held, a force of 2 N shall be applied to the apex of the triangle, parallel to the supporting surface and normal to the lower side of the triangle.
The apex of the triangle shall not move more than 5 cm in the direction in which the force is exerted.
After the test, the position of the device shall not be significantly different from its original position.
The advance warning triangle, in its protective cover if provided, shall be kept for 12 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 60 °C ± 2 °C.
After the test, no cracking or noticeable distortion of the device shall be visible; this applies in particular to the retro-reflective device.
The cover of the warning triangle shall be readily openable.
The cover shall not adhere to the warning triangle.
Immediately after removal from the cold room, no fractures or visible distortion shall be noticeable on the device, especially on its optical parts.
If a protective cover is provided, it shall be properly openable.
The protective cover shall neither tear nor adhere to the advance warning triangle.
The surface on which the test is to be carried out shall be dry.
The surface on which the test is to be carried out shall first be brushed with a soft brush to remove any dirt or loose gravel.
The advance warning triangle shall be set up in a wind tunnel.
The advance warning triangle shall be set up on a base measuring about 1.50 m by 1.20 m.
The surface of the base shall be formed of abrasive material of the type P36 corresponding to the FEPA specification 43‑1‑2006.
The base surface shall be characterised by a geometric roughness HS = 0.5 mm ± 0.05 mm.
The geometric roughness of the base surface shall be defined and determined by the so-called "sandy beach" method according to paragraph 4.
The base shall have a splitter plate.
The splitter plate on the base shall be provided to avoid a laminar boundary layer of the incident flow over the surface of the base.
The base shall be set up in such a way that the flow is completely around the splitter plate.
For the air flow, the air stream shall reach a dynamic pressure of 180 Pa.
For the air flow, the flow field shall be homogeneous and free of turbulence.

The dimension of the flow field shall be such that, horizontally to each corner and vertically to the top of the advance warning triangle, a clearance of at least 150 mm to the border line of the flow field exists.
The air stream (flow field) shall be parallel to the supporting surface, in the direction that seems most unfavourable for stability.
In the case of a closed wind tunnel, the area of the advance warning triangle shall not be larger than 5 per cent of the cross-sectional area of the closed wind tunnel.
When the advance warning triangle is set up in the manner specified in the preceding test set-up, it shall be subjected for 3 minutes to the open-air stream referred to in that set-up.
The advance warning triangle shall not overturn and shall not shift.
Slight shifting of the points of contact of the advance warning triangle with the road surface, by not more than 5 cm, is allowed.
The retro-reflecting triangular part of the device shall not rotate more than 10° about a horizontal axis or a vertical axis from its initial position.

The rotation of the retro-reflecting triangular part of the device about the horizontal axis or the vertical axis shall be determined using a virtual plane at its initial position that is orthogonal to the base and orthogonal to the air stream.
The approval number must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number must face the same way as the letter "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class must be diametrically opposite the approval number.
The Type Approval Authorities shall not use approval numbers IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA where they might be confused with the class symbols IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA.
Governments should require that slow-moving vehicles which, by construction, cannot travel faster than 30 km/h be fitted with rear marking plates for slow-moving vehicles and their trailers.

Rear marking plates for slow-moving vehicles and their trailers shall conform to this Regulation and to the specific requirements relating to its scope in accordance with the guidelines given in Annex 11.
The rear marking plate(s) shall be type approved.
The rear marking plate(s) shall meet the requirements of this Regulation.
The apex of a rear marking plate shall be directed upwards.
Every part of a rear marking plate shall lie within 5° of a transverse vertical plane at right angles to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
Every part of a rear marking plate shall face to the rear.
If there is only one rear marking plate, it must be on the opposite side of the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle to the direction of traffic prescribed in the country of registration.
The rear marking plate must be positioned above the ground, with its lower edge not less than 250 mm above the ground.
The rear marking plate must be positioned with its upper edge not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.
The rear marking plate must be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
The rear marking plate shall be geometrically visible within a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and 30° outwards.
Indispensable constructional parts of the vehicle may cover up to 10 per cent of the rear marking plate surface within the horizontal visibility angle.
The rear marking plate shall be geometrically visible within a vertical angle of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.
